sentences.zh: 乞伏國仁

translations.literal: Qifu Guoren
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Guoren (Western Qin)

sentences.zh: 乞伏國仁，隴西鮮卑人也。

translations.literal: Qifu Guoren was a Xianbei man of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Guoren was a Xianbei of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 在昔有如弗斯、出連、叱盧三部，自漠北南出大陰山，遇一巨蟲于路，狀若神龜，大如陵阜，乃殺馬而祭之，祝曰：「若善神也，便開路；

translations.literal: In antiquity the three divisions of Rufusi, Chulian, and Chilu came south from the northern deserts beyond the Great Yin Mountains; on the road they met a huge creature, shaped like a divine tortoise and as large as a tomb-mound; they killed a horse to sacrifice to it and prayed: "If you are a good spirit, then open the way;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Rufusi, Chulian, and Chilu clans marched south from the northern wastes beyond the Great Yin Mountains. On the road they met a colossal beast shaped like a sacred tortoise, as large as a tomb mound. They slaughtered a horse as an offering and prayed: "If you are a benevolent spirit, clear our path;

sentences.zh: 惡神也，遂塞不通。

translations.literal: if an evil spirit, then block it so we cannot pass."
translations.idiomatic: if you are malign, bar the way and let us go no farther."

sentences.zh: 」俄而不見，乃有一小兒在焉。

translations.literal: " In a moment it vanished, and there was a small child there.
translations.idiomatic: A moment later the creature was gone, and a small child stood there.

sentences.zh: 時又有乞伏部有老父無子者，請養為子，眾咸許之。

translations.literal: At that time there was also in the Qifu division an old man without a son who asked to adopt and raise him; the multitude all consented.
translations.idiomatic: An old man of the Qifu clan who had no son asked to adopt the child, and the assembly agreed.

sentences.zh: 老父欣然自以有所依憑，字之曰紇幹。

translations.literal: The old man gladly felt he now had something to rely on and gave him the childhood name Hegan.
translations.idiomatic: The old man rejoiced that he had gained a support and gave the boy the childhood name Hegan.

sentences.zh: 紇幹者，夏言依倚也。

translations.literal: Hegan means "to lean upon" in the Xia language.
translations.idiomatic: Hegan means "to lean upon" in the Xia tongue.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，驍勇善騎射，彎弓五百斤。

translations.literal: At age ten he was fierce and brave, skilled at riding and shooting, and could draw a bow of five hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he was already fierce in battle, expert at horsemanship and archery, and could bend a bow rated at five hundred jin.

sentences.zh: 四部服其雄武，推為統主，號之曰乞伏可汗托鐸莫何。

translations.literal: The four divisions submitted to his martial prowess and made him their chief, styling him Qifu Khan Tuoduo Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: All four divisions bowed to his valor and raised him as chief, styling him Qifu Khan Tuoduo Mohe.

sentences.zh: 托鐸者，言非神非人之稱也。

translations.literal: Tuoduo means a title neither of god nor of man.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoduo denotes a title that is neither divine nor human.

sentences.zh: 其後有祐鄰者，即國仁五世祖也。

translations.literal: Later there was Youlin, who was Guoren's fifth-generation ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Youlin, Guoren's fifth-generation forebear.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，率戶五千遷于夏緣，部眾稍盛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taishi era he led five thousand households to migrate to Xiayuan; the division gradually grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening years of Taishi he led five thousand households into Xiayuan, and the clan steadily grew in strength.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑鹿結七萬餘落，屯于高平川，與祐鄰迭相攻擊。

translations.literal: The Xianbei chief Lujie, with more than seventy thousand households, encamped on the Gaoping River and with Youlin attacked one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei leader Lujie, commanding more than seventy thousand households, camped on the Gaoping River and traded blows with Youlin.

sentences.zh: 鹿結敗，南奔略陽，祐鄰盡並其眾，固居高平川。

translations.literal: Lujie was defeated and fled south to Lueyang; Youlin absorbed all his followers and held firm on the Gaoping River.
translations.idiomatic: Lujie was beaten and fled south to Lueyang; Youlin absorbed his entire following and entrenched himself on the Gaoping River.

sentences.zh: 祐鄰死，子結權立，徙於牽屯。

translations.literal: Youlin died and his son Jiequan succeeded, moving the seat to Qiantun.
translations.idiomatic: When Youlin died his son Jiequan succeeded him and moved the seat to Qiantun.

sentences.zh: 結權死，子利那立，擊鮮卑吐賴于烏樹山，討尉遲渴權于大非川，收眾三萬餘落。

translations.literal: Jiequan died and his son Lina succeeded; he attacked the Xianbei chief Tulai at Wushu Mountain, campaigned against Yuchi Kequan at the Dafei River, and gathered more than thirty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Jiequan died and his son Lina took the throne. Lina struck the Xianbei chief Tulai at Wushu Mountain, campaigned against Yuchi Kequan on the Dafei River, and mustered more than thirty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 利那死，弟祁埿立。

translations.literal: Lina died and his younger brother Qimo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Lina died his younger brother Qimo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 祁埿死，利那子述延立。

translations.literal: Qimo died and Lina's son Shuyan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Qimo died, Lina's son Shuyan took the throne.

sentences.zh: 討鮮卑莫侯于苑川，大破之，降其眾二萬餘落，固居苑川。

translations.literal: He campaigned against the Xianbei chief Mohou at Yuanchuan, routed him utterly, received the submission of more than twenty thousand of his households, and settled firmly at Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan campaigned against the Xianbei chief Mohou at Yuanchuan, crushed him, accepted the surrender of more than twenty thousand households, and made Yuanchuan his base.

sentences.zh: 以叔父軻埿為師傅，委以國政，斯引烏埿為左輔將軍，鎮蔡園川，出連高胡為右輔將軍，鎮至便川，叱盧那胡為率義將軍，鎮牽屯山。

translations.literal: He made his uncle Kemo tutor, entrusted him with state affairs, appointed Siyin Wuqi Left Assistant General to garrison Caiyuanchuan, Chulian Gaohu Right Assistant General to garrison Zhibianchuan, and Chilu Nahua General Who Leads Righteousness to garrison Qiantun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He named his uncle Kemo tutor and entrusted him with government, made Siyin Wuqi Left Assistant General with a garrison at Caiyuanchuan, Chulian Gaohu Right Assistant General at Zhibianchuan, and Chilu Nahua General Who Leads Righteousness at Qiantun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 述延死，子傉大寒立。

translations.literal: Shuyan died and his son Lu Dahan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuyan died his son Lu Dahan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 會石勒滅劉曜，懼而遷于麥田無孤山。

translations.literal: When Shi Le destroyed Liu Yao, Lu Dahan, in fear, moved to the Mai Field and Wugu Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le destroyed Liu Yao, Lu Dahan, alarmed, relocated to the Mai Field and Wugu Mountains.

sentences.zh: 大寒死，子司繁立，始遷於度堅山。

translations.literal: Dahan died and his son Sifan succeeded; he first moved the seat to Dujian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Dahan died and his son Sifan succeeded, first moving the seat to Dujian Mountain.

sentences.zh: 尋為苻堅將王統所襲，部眾叛降於統。

translations.literal: Before long he was attacked by Fu Jian's general Wang Tong; his followers rebelled and surrendered to Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Fu Jian's general Wang Tong struck him; his followers defected and surrendered to Tong.

sentences.zh: 司繁歎謂左右曰：「智不距敵，德不撫眾，劍騎未交而本根已敗，見眾分散，勢亦難全。

translations.literal: Sifan sighed and said to those beside him: "Wisdom cannot withstand the enemy, virtue cannot comfort the masses; before swords and horsemen had met, the root was already broken. Seeing the host scattered, the situation is hard to preserve intact.
translations.idiomatic: Sifan sighed to his attendants: "Wisdom cannot match the foe, virtue cannot hold the host together—before blade met blade our foundation was lost. With the army scattered, how can we survive intact?

sentences.zh: 若奔諸部，必不我容，吾將為呼韓邪之計矣。

translations.literal: If I flee to the other divisions they surely will not receive me; I shall adopt the plan of Huhanxie."
translations.idiomatic: If I flee to the other clans they will not shelter me. I must take Huhanxie's course."

sentences.zh: 」乃詣統降於堅。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he went to Tong and surrendered to Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Tong and submitted to Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 堅大悅，署為南單于，留之長安。

translations.literal: Fu Jian was greatly pleased, appointed him Southern Chanyu, and kept him at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was greatly pleased, named him Southern Chanyu, and detained him at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 以司繁叔父吐雷為勇士護軍，撫其部眾。

translations.literal: He made Sifan's uncle Tulei Warrior Protector General to pacify his tribal following.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Sifan's uncle Tulei Warrior Protector General to pacify the tribal following.

sentences.zh: 俄而鮮卑勃寒侵斥隴右，堅以司繁為使持節、都督討西胡諸軍事、鎮西將軍以討之。

translations.literal: Before long the Xianbei chief Bo Han invaded and pressed Longyou; Fu Jian made Sifan Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief for Campaigns against the Western Hu, and General Who Pacifies the West to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Xianbei chief Bo Han raided Longyou. Fu Jian made Sifan Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief for Campaigns against the Western Hu, and General Who Pacifies the West to subdue him.

sentences.zh: 勃寒懼而請降，司繁遂鎮勇士川，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: Bo Han, in fear, requested surrender; Sifan then garrisoned Warrior River and was very effective in authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Han, terrified, sued for peace. Sifan garrisoned Warrior River and ruled with stern authority and generous kindness.

sentences.zh: 司繁卒，國仁代鎮，及堅興壽春之役，徵為前將軍，領先鋒騎。

translations.literal: When Sifan died, Guoren replaced him in the garrison; when Fu Jian launched the Shouchun campaign, Guoren was summoned as Forward General and led the vanguard cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After Sifan's death Guoren took his garrison. When Fu Jian marched on Shouchun, Guoren was summoned as Forward General to lead the vanguard horse.

sentences.zh: 會國仁叔父步頹叛於隴西，堅遣國仁還討之。

translations.literal: At that time Guoren's uncle Bufei rebelled in Longxi; Fu Jian sent Guoren back to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren's uncle Bufei rebelled in Longxi, and Fu Jian sent Guoren back to crush the revolt.

sentences.zh: 步頹聞而大悅，迎國仁于路。

translations.literal: Bufei heard this and was greatly pleased; he welcomed Guoren on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Bufei heard the news with delight and went out to welcome Guoren on the road.

sentences.zh: 國仁置酒高會，攘袂大言曰：「苻氏往因趙石之亂，遂妄竊名號，窮兵極武，跨僭八州。

translations.literal: Guoren set out wine for a grand gathering, rolled up his sleeves, and spoke loudly: "The Fu clan, riding on the chaos of Zhao and Shi, then presumptuously seized titles, exhausted the armies to the utmost in warfare, and usurped authority across eight provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren held a feast, rolled up his sleeves, and declared: "The Fu seized their chance in the chaos of Later Zhao, usurped the throne, exhausted every army, and claimed eight provinces by force.

sentences.zh: 疆宇既寧，宜綏以德，方虛廣威聲，勤心遠略，騷動蒼生，疲弊中國，違天怒人，將何以濟！

translations.literal: Now that the realm is settled they ought to soothe it with virtue; instead they hollow out their prestige, strain after distant schemes, disturb the common people, wear out the Middle Kingdom, defy Heaven and anger men—how can they succeed!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is pacified, yet they rule by terror instead of virtue, hollow out their prestige, and harass the people until the heartland groans—defying Heaven and enraging men. How can such a house endure?

sentences.zh: 且物極則虧、禍盈而覆者，天之道也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when things reach their extreme they decline; when misfortune is full it overturns—such is Heaven's way.
translations.idiomatic: When fortune peaks it turns; when calamity fills the cup it spills—that is Heaven's way.

sentences.zh: 以吾量之，是役也，難以免矣。

translations.literal: By my reckoning, in this campaign escape will be hard.
translations.idiomatic: By my reckoning they cannot escape defeat in this campaign.

sentences.zh: 當與諸君成一方之業。

translations.literal: I shall with you all accomplish a regional enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: Let us together build a realm of our own."

sentences.zh: 」及堅敗歸，乃招集諸部，有不附者，討而並之，眾至十餘萬。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian returned defeated, Guoren then summoned the various divisions; those who would not submit he campaigned against and absorbed, until his host reached more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian fled home in defeat, Guoren rallied the clans, subdued those who held back, and swelled his host to more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 及堅為姚萇所殺，國仁謂其豪帥曰：「苻氏以高世之姿而困於烏合之眾，可謂天也。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian was killed by Yao Chang, Guoren said to his tribal chiefs: "The Fu clan, with the stature of transcending the age, was trapped by a mob gathering—one may call this Heaven's doing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang killed Fu Jian, Guoren told his chiefs: "The Fu stood above their age yet fell to a rabble—surely Heaven decreed it.

sentences.zh: 夫守常迷運，先達恥之；

translations.literal: To cling to the constant and miss the turning of fortune—men of foresight are ashamed of it;
translations.idiomatic: To cling to routine when fortune turns is shameful to the wise;

sentences.zh: 見機而作，英豪之舉。

translations.literal: to see the moment and act is the deed of heroes.
translations.idiomatic: to seize the moment is the mark of heroes.

sentences.zh: 吾雖薄德，藉累世之資，豈可睹時來之運而不作乎！

translations.literal: Though my virtue is slight, relying on the resources of many generations, how can I watch fortune arrive and not act!"
translations.idiomatic: My virtue is slight, but generations of strength lie behind me—how can I watch fortune arrive and do nothing!"

sentences.zh: 」以孝武自稱大都督、大將軍、大單于、領秦、河二州牧，建元曰建義。

translations.literal: He took the reign title of Emperor Xiaowu for himself, styled himself Grand Commander, Grand General, and Grand Chanyu, and held the governorships of Qin and He provinces; his era name was Jianyi.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself Grand Commander, Grand General, and Grand Chanyu, took the reign title of Emperor Xiaowu, governed Qin and He provinces, and proclaimed the era Jianyi.

sentences.zh: 以其將乙旃音埿為左相，屋引出支為右相，獨孤匹蹄為左輔，武群勇士為右輔，弟乾歸為上將軍，自余拜授各有差。

translations.literal: He made his generals Yizhan Yinyi Left Chancellor, Wuyin Chuzhi Right Chancellor, Dugu Piti Left Assistant, Wuqun Yongshi Right Assistant, and his younger brother Gangui General-in-Chief; the rest received appointments in varying grades.
translations.idiomatic: He named Yizhan Yinyi Left Chancellor, Wuyin Chuzhi Right Chancellor, Dugu Piti Left Assistant, Wuqun Yongshi Right Assistant, and his younger brother Gangui General-in-Chief; the remainder received ranks as merit allowed.

sentences.zh: 置武城、武陽、安固、武始、漢陽、天水、略陽、漒川、甘松、匡朋、白馬、苑川十二郡，築勇士城以居之。

translations.literal: He established twelve commanderies—Wucheng, Wuyang, Angu, Wushi, Hanyang, Tianshui, Lueyang, Qiangchuan, Gansong, Kuangpeng, Baima, and Yuanchuan—and built Warrior City to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: He carved out twelve commanderies—Wucheng, Wuyang, Angu, Wushi, Hanyang, Tianshui, Lueyang, Qiangchuan, Gansong, Kuangpeng, Baima, and Yuanchuan—and built Warrior City as his capital.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑匹蘭率眾五千降。

translations.literal: The Xianbei chief Pilan led five thousand followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei chief Pilan surrendered with five thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 明年，南安秘宜及諸羌虜來擊國仁，四面而至。

translations.literal: The next year the Nan'an leader Miyi and various Qiang and Di raiders attacked Guoren, coming from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Miyi of Nan'an and allied Qiang and Di forces struck Guoren from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 國仁謂諸將曰：「先人有奪人之心，不可坐待其至。

translations.literal: Guoren said to his generals: "Our forebears had the heart to seize from others; we cannot sit and wait for them to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren told his generals: "Our forebears seized the initiative; we must not wait for the enemy to reach us.

sentences.zh: 宜抑威餌敵，羸師以張之，軍法所謂怒我而怠寇也。

translations.literal: We should lower our pride to bait the enemy, show a weakened force to inflate their confidence—what the military codes call making the foe angry at us while they grow slack."
translations.idiomatic: Lower your banners to bait them, parade a weakened host to swell their pride—that is what the manuals call angering ourselves to slacken the foe."

sentences.zh: 」於是勒眾五千，襲其不意，大敗之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he marshaled five thousand men, struck where they did not expect, and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered five thousand men, struck where they did not expect, and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 秘宜奔還南安，尋與其弟莫侯悌率眾三萬餘戶降于國仁，各拜將軍、刺史。

translations.literal: Miyi fled back to Nan'an; soon he and his younger brother Mohouti led more than thirty thousand households to surrender to Guoren, and each was appointed general and inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Miyi fled to Nan'an; soon he and his brother Mohouti surrendered with more than thirty thousand households, and Guoren named each a general and inspector.

sentences.zh: 苻登遣使者署國仁使持節、大都督、都督雜夷諸軍事、大將軍、大單于、苑川王。

translations.literal: Fu Deng sent envoys to appoint Guoren Bearer of the Staff, Grand Commander, Commander-in-Chief of the Various Yi, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng sent envoys appointing Guoren Bearer of the Staff, Grand Commander, Commander-in-Chief of the Various Yi, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 國仁率騎三萬襲鮮卑大人密貴、裕苟、提倫等三部於六泉。

translations.literal: Guoren led thirty thousand horsemen to strike the Xianbei great chiefs Migui, Yugou, and Tilun and their three divisions at Liuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren led thirty thousand horse against the Xianbei chiefs Migui, Yugou, and Tilun and their three divisions at Liuquan.

sentences.zh: 高平鮮卑沒奕于、東胡金熙連兵來襲，相遇於渴渾川，大戰敗之，斬級三千，獲馬五千匹。

translations.literal: The Gaoping Xianbei chief Moyu and the Eastern Hu chief Jin Xi joined forces to attack; they met at Kehun River, fought a great battle, defeated them, beheaded three thousand, and captured five thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoping Xianbei Moyu and the Eastern Hu Jin Xi joined forces to attack. At Kehun River Guoren met them in battle, crushed them, took three thousand heads, and seized five thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 沒奕於及熙奔還，三部震懼，率眾迎降。

translations.literal: Moyu and Jin Xi fled back; the three divisions were terrified and led their masses to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Moyu and Jin Xi fled; the three divisions, terrified, came in submission.

sentences.zh: 署密貴建義將軍、六泉侯，裕苟建忠將軍、蘭泉侯，提倫建節將軍、鳴泉侯。

translations.literal: He appointed Migui General Who Establishes Righteousness and Marquis of Liuquan, Yugou General Who Establishes Loyalty and Marquis of Lanquan, and Tilun General Who Establishes Integrity and Marquis of Mingquan.
translations.idiomatic: He named Migui General Who Establishes Righteousness and Marquis of Liuquan, Yugou General Who Establishes Loyalty and Marquis of Lanquan, and Tilun General Who Establishes Integrity and Marquis of Mingquan.

sentences.zh: 國仁建威將軍叱盧烏孤跋擁眾叛，保牽屯山。

translations.literal: Guoren's General Who Establishes Prestige Chilu Wugu Ba led his followers in rebellion and held Qiantun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren's General Who Establishes Prestige, Chilu Wugu Ba, rebelled with his following and held Qiantun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 國仁率騎七千討之，斬其部將叱羅侯，降者千餘戶。

translations.literal: Guoren led seven thousand horsemen to campaign against him, beheaded his divisional officer Chiluo Hou, and more than a thousand households surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren led seven thousand horse against him, slew his officer Chiluo Hou, and won the surrender of more than a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 跋大懼，遂降，復其官位。

translations.literal: Ba was greatly afraid and then surrendered; Guoren restored his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Ba submitted; Guoren restored his titles.

sentences.zh: 因討鮮卑越質叱黎于平襄，大破之，獲其子詰歸、弟子復半及部落五千餘人而還。

translations.literal: He then campaigned against the Xianbei chief Yuezhi Chilu at Pingxiang, routed him utterly, captured his son Jiegui, his younger brother's son Fuban, and more than five thousand of the tribe, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then struck the Xianbei chief Yuezhi Chilu at Pingxiang, crushed him, took his son Jiegui, his nephew Fuban, and more than five thousand of the tribe, and returned.

sentences.zh: ，國仁死，在位四年，偽諡宣烈王，廟號烈祖。

translations.literal: , Guoren died; he had ruled four years; his posthumous title was King Xuanlie; his temple name was Liezu.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren died after four years on the throne. His posthumous title was King Xuanlie; his temple name was Liezu.

sentences.zh: 乞伏-{乾}-歸

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui (Gangui)

sentences.zh: -{乾}-歸，國仁弟也。

translations.literal: Gangui was Guoren's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui, Guoren's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 雄武英傑，沈雅有度量。

translations.literal: Heroic and martial, a brilliant man, deep and refined in bearing with great magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: He was heroic and brilliant, reserved in manner and broad in judgment.

sentences.zh: 國仁之死也，其群臣咸以國仁子公府沖幼，宜立長君，乃推乾歸為大都督、大將軍、大單于、河南王，赦其境內，改元曰太初。

translations.literal: At Guoren's death his ministers all considered Guoren's son Gongfu too young in years; they ought to establish an elder lord, and so they pushed Gangui to be Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Henan; he granted amnesty within his borders and changed the era name to Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: When Guoren died his ministers judged his son Gongfu too young and raised Gangui as Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Henan. He proclaimed an amnesty and adopted the era Taichu.

sentences.zh: 立其妻邊氏為王后，以出連乞都為丞相，鎮南將軍、南梁州刺史悌眷為御史大夫，自余封拜各有差。

translations.literal: He made his wife the Lady Bian queen, appointed Chulian Qidu Chancellor, and made the General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Southern Liangzhou Tijuan Censor-in-Chief; the rest received enfeoffments and appointments in varying grades.
translations.idiomatic: He made Lady Bian his queen, named Chulian Qidu Chancellor, and appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Southern Liang Tijuan Censor-in-Chief; the rest received titles as rank allowed.

sentences.zh: 遂遷于金城。

translations.literal: He then moved the capital to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved the seat to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: ，苻登遣使署乾歸大將軍、大單于、金城王。

translations.literal: , Fu Deng sent envoys to appoint Gangui Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng sent envoys appointing Gangui Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 南羌獨如率眾七千降之。

translations.literal: The Southern Qiang chief Duru led seven thousand followers to surrender to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Qiang chief Duru surrendered with seven thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 休官阿敦、侯年二部各擁五千餘落，據牽屯山，為其邊害。

translations.literal: The Xiuguan divisions of Adun and Hounian, each with more than five thousand households, held Qiantun Mountain and harried his borders.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiuguan clans of Adun and Hounian, each numbering more than five thousand households, held Qiantun Mountain and plagued his frontier.

sentences.zh: 乾歸討破之，悉降其眾，於是聲振邊服。

translations.literal: Gangui campaigned against and defeated them, wholly receiving the submission of their masses; his renown then shook the borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui crushed them and accepted the surrender of their entire following; his fame then resounded along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾大人視連遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun great chief Shilian sent envoys bearing tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun chief Shilian sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑豆留䩭、叱豆渾及南丘鹿結並休官曷呼奴、盧水尉地跋並率眾降於乾歸，皆署其官爵。

translations.literal: The Xianbei chiefs Douliumi, Chidouhun, and Nanqiu Lujie, together with the Xiuguan chiefs Hehunu and Lu Shui Weidiba, all led their followings to surrender to Gangui; he appointed each to office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei chiefs Douliumi, Chidouhun, and Nanqiu Lujie, with the Xiuguan chiefs Hehunu and Lu Shui Weidiba, all submitted with their followings; Gangui invested each with office and rank.

sentences.zh: 隴西太守越質詰歸以平襄叛，自稱建國將軍、右賢王。

translations.literal: The Longxi Administrator Yuezhi Jiegui rebelled at Pingxiang, styling himself General Who Establishes the State and Right Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi administrator Yuezhi Jiegui rebelled at Pingxiang and styled himself General Who Establishes the State and Right Worthy King.

sentences.zh: 幹歸擊敗之，詰歸東奔隴山。

translations.literal: Gangui struck and defeated him; Jiegui fled east to Longshan.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui defeated him; Jiegui fled east to Longshan.

sentences.zh: 既而擁眾來降，乾歸妻以宗女，署立義將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he led his masses to come and surrender; Gangui gave him a clanswoman in marriage and appointed him General Who Establishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiegui returned with his following; Gangui married him to a clanswoman and named him General Who Establishes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 苻登將沒奕於遣使結好，以二子為質，請討鮮卑大兜國。

translations.literal: Fu Deng's general Moyu sent envoys to form an alliance, offering his two sons as hostages and requesting a joint campaign against the Xianbei chief Dadou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng's general Moyu sent envoys seeking alliance, offering his two sons as hostages and asking Gangui to join him against the Xianbei chief Dadou.

sentences.zh: 乾歸乃與沒奕於攻大兜於安陽城，大兜退固鳴蟬堡，乾歸攻陷之，遂還金城。

translations.literal: Gangui then joined Moyu in attacking Dadou at Anyang City; Dadou withdrew and held fast at Mingchan Fort; Gangui stormed and took it, then returned to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui joined Moyu in attacking Dadou at Anyang. Dadou retreated to Mingchan Fort; Gangui stormed the fort and returned to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 為呂光弟寶所攻，敗於鳴雀峽，退屯青岸。

translations.literal: He was attacked by Lü Guang's younger brother Bao, was defeated at Mingque Gorge, and withdrew to encamp at Qing'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang's brother Bao attacked him; Gangui was beaten at Mingque Gorge and withdrew to Qing'an.

sentences.zh: 寶進追乾歸，乾歸使其將彭奚念斷其歸路，躬貫甲胄，連戰敗之，寶及將士投河死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Bao pressed the pursuit; Gangui had his general Peng Xinian cut off Bao's line of retreat, personally donned armor, fought in succession and defeated him; Bao and his officers and soldiers, more than ten thousand, threw themselves into the river and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Bao pressed the pursuit. Gangui sent Peng Xinian to sever his retreat, donned armor himself, and fought him down in successive clashes. Bao and more than ten thousand soldiers drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 苻登遣使署乾歸假黃鉞、大都督隴右河西諸軍事、左丞相、大將軍、河南王，領秦、梁、益、涼、沙五州牧，加九錫之禮。

translations.literal: Fu Deng sent envoys to appoint Gangui Acting Bearer of the Yellow Axe, Grand Commander of the Longyou and Hexi Armies, Left Chancellor, Grand General, Prince of Henan, Governor of Qin, Liang, Yi, Liang, and Sha provinces, with the nine bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng sent envoys appointing Gangui Acting Bearer of the Yellow Axe, Grand Commander of the Longyou and Hexi Armies, Left Chancellor, Grand General, Prince of Henan, Governor of Qin, Liang, Yi, Liang, and Sha, with the nine bestowals.

sentences.zh: 時登為姚興所逼，遣使請兵，進封乾歸梁王，命置官司，納其妹東平長公主為梁王后。

translations.literal: At that time Deng was pressed by Yao Xing and sent envoys requesting troops; he advanced Gangui to Prince of Liang, ordered him to establish offices, and gave him his younger sister the Princess of Eastern Peace as Princess of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng, hard pressed by Yao Xing, begged for troops, advanced Gangui to Prince of Liang, ordered him to set up a full court, and gave him his sister the Princess of Eastern Peace as consort.

sentences.zh: 乾歸遣其前將軍乞伏益州、冠軍翟瑥率騎二萬救之。

translations.literal: Gangui sent his Forward General Qifu Yizhou and Champion Zhai Wei with twenty thousand horsemen to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui sent Forward General Qifu Yizhou and Champion Zhai Wei with twenty thousand horse to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 會登為興所殺，乃還師。

translations.literal: When Deng was killed by Yao Xing, they withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xing killed Deng, they marched home.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊定率步騎四萬伐之。

translations.literal: The Di king Yang Ding led forty thousand foot and horse to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Di king Yang Ding marched against him with forty thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 乾歸謂諸將曰：「楊定以勇虐聚眾，窮兵逞欲。

translations.literal: Gangui said to his generals: "Yang Ding gathers followers through courage and cruelty and exhausts the armies to indulge his desires.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui told his generals: "Yang Ding rules by brutality, gathering men through fear and exhausting armies for his appetites.

sentences.zh: 兵猶火也，不戢，將自焚。

translations.literal: Armies are like fire; if not checked, they will burn themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Armies are like fire—unchecked, they consume themselves.

sentences.zh: 定之此役，殆天以之資我也。

translations.literal: In this campaign of Ding's, Heaven is surely furnishing us resources."
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign Heaven is surely handing us Yang Ding's strength."

sentences.zh: 」於是遣其涼州牧乞伏軻殫、秦州牧乞伏益州、立義將軍詰歸距之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent his Governor of Liangzhou Qifu Kedan, Governor of Qinzhou Qifu Yizhou, and General Who Establishes Righteousness Jiegui to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Governor of Liangzhou Qifu Kedan, Governor of Qinzhou Qifu Yizhou, and General Who Establishes Righteousness Jiegui to meet him.

sentences.zh: 定敗益州于平川，軻殫、詰歸引眾而退。

translations.literal: Ding defeated Yizhou at Pingchuan; Kedan and Jiegui led their masses in withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Ding beat Yizhou at Pingchuan; Kedan and Jiegui drew off their forces.

sentences.zh: 翟瑥奮劍諫曰：「吾王以神武之姿，開基隴右，東征西討，靡不席捲，威震秦、梁，聲光巴、漢。

translations.literal: Zhai Wei, flourishing his sword, remonstrated: "Our king, with divine martial bearing, founded his base in Longyou; east and west he campaigned, and nothing escaped his sweep; his might shook Qin and Liang, his fame reached Ba and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Wei drew his sword and protested: "Our king, born to command, founded his realm in Longyou and swept east and west until Qin and Liang trembled and Ba and Han took notice.

sentences.zh: 將軍以維城之重，受閫外之寄，宜宣力致命，輔甯家國。

translations.literal: You, general, bear the weight of guarding the walls, have received trust beyond the passes—you ought to exert your strength unto death and assist in securing the house and state.
translations.idiomatic: You bear the weight of the realm's defense and hold command beyond the passes—you should spend your life in the king's service and secure the state.

sentences.zh: 秦州雖敗，二軍猶全，奈何不思直救，便逆奔敗，何面目以見王乎！

translations.literal: Though Qinzhou was defeated, the two armies are still intact—how can you not think to go straight to the rescue but instead turn and flee in defeat? With what face will you see the king!
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou fell, but two armies remain intact—why not rush to their aid instead of fleeing in defeat? What face will you show the king?

sentences.zh: 昔項羽斬慶子以甯楚，胡建戮監軍以成功，將軍之所聞也。

translations.literal: In old times Xiang Yu beheaded Qingzi to secure Chu; Hu Jian executed the army supervisor to achieve success—things the general has heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu slew Qingzi to save Chu; Hu Jian executed the army supervisor to win victory—you have heard such tales.

sentences.zh: 瑥誠才非古人，敢忘項氏之義乎！

translations.literal: Wei's talent is truly not that of the ancients, yet dare I forget the righteousness of the Xiang clan!"
translations.idiomatic: My talent falls short of the ancients, yet how dare I forget the House of Xiang's example!"

sentences.zh: 」軻殫曰：「向所以未赴秦州者，未知眾心何如耳。

translations.literal: " Kedan said: "The reason I did not go to Qinzhou earlier was that I did not know how the masses' hearts stood.
translations.idiomatic: Kedan replied: "I held back from Qinzhou because I did not yet know where the army's heart lay.

sentences.zh: 敗不相救，軍罰所先，敢自寧乎！

translations.literal: Not to rescue one another in defeat is what military punishment strikes first—how dare I seek my own ease!
translations.idiomatic: To abandon comrades in defeat is the first crime under military law—how could I seek my own comfort?

sentences.zh: 」乃率騎赴之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led his horsemen to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his cavalry to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 益州、詰歸亦勒眾而進，大敗定，斬定及首虜萬七千級。

translations.literal: Yizhou and Jiegui also marshaled their masses and advanced; they routed Ding utterly, beheaded Ding, and took seventeen thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou and Jiegui marched in turn, crushed Yang Ding, slew him, and took seventeen thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 於是盡有隴西、巴西之地。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wholly possessed the lands of Longxi and Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: He thus held all of Longxi and Baxi.

sentences.zh: ，赦其境內殊死以下，署其長子熾磐領尚書令，左長史邊芮為尚書左僕射，右長史秘宜為右僕射，翟瑥為吏部尚書，翟勍為主客尚書，杜宣為兵部尚書，王松壽為民部尚書，樊謙為三公尚書，方弘、麹景為侍中，自余拜授一如魏武、晉文故事。

translations.literal: , He granted amnesty within his borders to all below the death penalty, appointed his eldest son Chipan to hold the office of Director of the Secretariat, made Left Chief Clerk Bian Rui Vice Director of the Left, Right Chief Clerk Miyi Vice Director of the Right, Zhai Wei Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Zhai Qing Director of the Ministry of Guests, Du Xuan Director of the Ministry of War, Wang Songshou Director of the Ministry of the People, Fan Qian Director of the Three Offices, Fang Hong and Qu Jing Attendants-in-Ordinary, and for the rest appointments followed the precedents of Cao Wu and Jin Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed an amnesty short of capital crimes, named his eldest son Chipan Director of the Secretariat, Bian Rui Vice Director of the Left, Miyi Vice Director of the Right, and filled the ministries and court ranks on the model of Cao Cao and Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 猶稱大單于、大將軍。

translations.literal: He still styled himself Grand Chanyu and Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He still bore the titles Grand Chanyu and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 楊定之死也，天水薑乳襲據上邽。

translations.literal: When Yang Ding died, the Tianshui man Jiang Ru seized and held Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Ding's death Jiang Ru of Tianshui seized Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 至是，遣乞伏益州討之。

translations.literal: At this time Gangui sent Qifu Yizhou to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui then sent Qifu Yizhou against him.

sentences.zh: 邊芮、王松壽言於乾歸曰：「益州以懿弟之親，屢有戰功，狃於累勝，常有驕色。

translations.literal: Bian Rui and Wang Songshou said to Gangui: "Yizhou, by reason of close kinship to your majesty's younger brother, has repeatedly won in battle and, trusting in successive victories, often shows arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Rui and Wang Songshou warned Gangui: "Yizhou is your brother's man and has grown proud on repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 若其遇寇，必將易之。

translations.literal: If he meets the enemy he is sure to take them lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting the foe he will surely underestimate them.

sentences.zh: 且未宜專任，示有所先。

translations.literal: Moreover it is not fitting to give him sole command—one should show that someone takes precedence over him."
translations.idiomatic: Do not give him sole command; let him see that others stand above him."

sentences.zh: 」乾歸曰：「益州驍勇，善禦眾，諸將莫有及之者，但恐其專擅耳。

translations.literal: " Gangui said: "Yizhou is fierce and brave, skilled at controlling the masses; among the generals none can match him—only I fear he may act on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui replied: "Yizhou is the boldest captain I have and masters the host—only I fear his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 若以重佐輔之，當無慮也。

translations.literal: If heavy assistants support him, there should be no worry."
translations.idiomatic: Pair him with weighty deputies and he will do."

sentences.zh: 」於是以平北韋虔為長史、散騎常侍務和為司馬。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he made Pingbei Wei Qian chief clerk and Attendant-in-Ordinary Wu He marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He named Wei Qian chief clerk and Wu He marshal.

sentences.zh: 至大寒嶺，益州恃勝自矜，不為部陣，命將士解甲遊畋縱飲，令曰：「敢言軍事者斬！

translations.literal: When they reached Dahan Ridge, Yizhou, trusting in victory, grew self-important, made no battle formation, ordered officers and soldiers to doff armor and roam hunting and drinking freely, and proclaimed: "Whoever speaks of military affairs shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: At Dahan Ridge Yizhou, drunk on victory, formed no battle line, let his men hunt and feast, and decreed death for anyone who spoke of war.

sentences.zh: 」虔等諫曰：「王以將軍親重，故委以專征之任，庶能摧彼凶醜，以副具瞻。

translations.literal: " Qian and the others remonstrated: "The king, because the general enjoys close and heavy favor, entrusted him with sole command on campaign, hoping he might crush those villains and answer what all look to.
translations.idiomatic: Qian protested: "The king gave you sole command to destroy the foe, not to feast.

sentences.zh: 賊已垂逼，奈何解甲自寬，宴安耽毒，竊為將軍危之。

translations.literal: The bandits are already pressing close—how can you doff armor and ease yourselves, feasting in indolent poison? I venture to say this is perilous for the general."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is upon us—why strip armor for sport? This will ruin you."

sentences.zh: 」益州曰：「乳以烏合之眾，聞吾至，理應遠竄。

translations.literal: " Yizhou said: "Ru leads a mob gathering; hearing that I have come, by rights he ought to flee far away.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou scoffed: "Ru is a rabble—he should run when he hears I am coming.

sentences.zh: 今乃與吾決戰者，斯成擒也。

translations.literal: That he now joins battle with me means he is ripe for capture."
translations.idiomatic: If he fights, he is already ours."

sentences.zh: 吾自揣之有方，卿等不足慮也。

translations.literal: "I myself have my measures; you need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: I have my plan; fret not."

sentences.zh: 」乳率眾距戰，益州果敗。

translations.literal: " Ru led his masses to resist in battle; Yizhou was indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ru gave battle and Yizhou was routed.

sentences.zh: 乾歸曰：「孤違蹇叔，以至於此。

translations.literal: Gangui said: "I went against Jian Shu and came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui said: "I ignored good counsel like Jian Shu—and here we are.

sentences.zh: 將士何為，孤之罪也。

translations.literal: What fault is it of the officers and soldiers? It is my crime."
translations.idiomatic: The fault is mine, not the troops'."

sentences.zh: 」皆赦之。

translations.literal: He pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: All were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 索虜禿髮如苟，率戶二萬降之，乾歸妻以宗女。

translations.literal: The Suo barbarian chief Tufa Rugou led twenty thousand households to surrender; Gangui gave him a clanswoman in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Rugou of the Suo tribes surrendered with twenty thousand households; Gangui married him to a kinswoman.

sentences.zh: 呂光率眾十萬將伐乾歸，左輔密貴周、左衛莫者羖羝言於乾歸曰：「光旦夕將至。

translations.literal: Lü Guang led a host of a hundred thousand intending to attack Gangui; Left Assistant Migui Zhou and Left Guard Moze Gudi said to Gangui: "Guang will arrive any day now.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang marched with a hundred thousand men. Migui Zhou and Moze Gudi urged Gangui: "Guang is almost here.

sentences.zh: 陛下以命世雄姿，開業洮罕，克翦群光，威振遐邇，將鼓淳風于東夏，建八百之鴻慶。

translations.literal: Your majesty, with the heroic stature of one destined for the age, has opened your enterprise at Tao and Han, cut down rival lights, and shaken the distant realms—you would plant pure customs in the eastern lands and establish the great blessing of eight hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: You were born to rule, built power on the Tao and Han rivers, and shattered rivals—why wrestle with a petty foe now?

sentences.zh: 不忍小下屈，與奸豎兢于一時，若機事不捷，非國家利也。

translations.literal: It is unworthy of a lesser power to bend and compete with a villain at one stroke; if the opportunity fails, it will not benefit the state.
translations.idiomatic: Bending to fight him on even terms risks the realm if fortune turns.

sentences.zh: 宜遣愛子以退之。

translations.literal: You should send a beloved son to make him withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Send a son as hostage and he will withdraw."

sentences.zh: 」乾歸乃稱籓於光，遣子敕勃為質。

translations.literal: " Gangui then declared himself a vassal of Guang and sent his son Chibo as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui submitted to Guang and sent his son Chibo as hostage.

sentences.zh: 既而悔之，遂誅周等。

translations.literal: Before long he regretted it and put Zhou and the others to death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he repented and executed Zhou and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 乞伏軻殫與乞伏益州不平，奔于呂光。

translations.literal: Qifu Kedan was on bad terms with Qifu Yizhou and fled to Lü Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Kedan, at odds with Yizhou, defected to Lü Guang.

sentences.zh: 光又伐之，咸勸其東奔成紀，乾歸不從，謂諸將曰：「昔曹孟德敗袁本初於官渡，陸伯言摧劉玄德于白帝，皆以權略取之，豈在眾乎！

translations.literal: Guang attacked again; all urged Gangui to flee east to Chengji, but Gangui would not follow and said to his generals: "In old times Cao Mengde defeated Yuan Benchu at Guandu, and Lu Boyan crushed Liu Xuande at Baidi—both took them by stratagem; does it lie in numbers!
translations.idiomatic: All urged flight to Chengji; Gangui refused: "Cao Cao beat Yuan Shao at Guandu and Lu Xun broke Liu Bei at Baidi by stratagem, not numbers!

sentences.zh: 光雖舉全州之軍，而無經遠之算，不足憚也。

translations.literal: Though Guang has raised the armies of a whole province, he has no far-reaching plan and is not to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Guang commands a province but lacks distant vision—he is no terror.

sentences.zh: 且其精卒盡在呂延，延雖勇而愚，易以奇策制之。

translations.literal: Moreover his crack troops are all with Lü Yan; though Yan is brave he is stupid and can be controlled by unorthodox plans.
translations.idiomatic: His best troops are with Lü Yan—brave but stupid, ripe for a ruse.

sentences.zh: 延軍若敗，光亦遁還，乘勝追奔，可以得志。

translations.literal: If Yan's army is defeated, Guang too will flee back; pursuing the victory we can fulfill our aim."
translations.idiomatic: Break Yan and Guang will flee; pursue and we prevail."

sentences.zh: 」眾咸曰：「非所及也。

translations.literal: " The multitude all said: "Not what we can reach."
translations.idiomatic: The officers murmured that it was beyond them.

sentences.zh: 」隆安元年，光遣其子纂伐乾歸，使呂延為前鋒。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Longan, Guang sent his son Zuan to attack Gangui, making Lü Yan vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In Longan year 1 Guang sent his son Zuan against Gangui with Lü Yan in the van.

sentences.zh: 乾歸泣謂眾曰：「今事勢窮踧，逃命無所，死中求生，正在今日。

translations.literal: Gangui wept and said to the host: "Now the situation is desperate and cramped; there is nowhere to flee for life—seeking life in death lies in this day alone.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui wept to his men: "We are cornered with nowhere to run—life today must be won from death.

sentences.zh: 涼軍雖四面而至，然相去遼遠，山河既阻，力不周接，敗其一軍而眾軍自退。

translations.literal: Though the Liang armies come from all four sides, they are far apart; rivers and mountains block them and their strength cannot join—defeat one army and the rest will withdraw of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Their columns are far apart and rivers block them—break one wing and the rest will melt away."

sentences.zh: 」乃縱反間，稱秦王乾歸眾潰，東奔成紀。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he spread false intelligence, saying King Gangui's host had scattered and fled east to Chengji.
translations.idiomatic: He spread word that Gangui's army had broken and fled toward Chengji.

sentences.zh: 延信之，引師輕進，果為乾歸所敗，遂斬之。

translations.literal: Yan believed it, led his army forward lightly, and was indeed defeated by Gangui; Gangui then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan swallowed the tale, advanced rashly, and Gangui destroyed him and took his head.

sentences.zh: 禿髮烏孤遣使來結和親。

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu sent envoys to conclude a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu sent envoys to seal a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 使乞伏益州攻克支陽、鸇武、允吾三城，俘獲萬餘人而還。

translations.literal: He sent Qifu Yizhou to capture the three cities of Zhiyang, Guanwu, and Yunwu, capturing more than ten thousand and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou took Zhiyang, Guanwu, and Yunwu with more than ten thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 又遣益州與武衛慕容允、冠軍翟瑥率騎二萬伐吐谷渾視羆，至於度周川，大破之。

translations.literal: He also sent Yizhou with Guard of the Martial Host Murong Yun and Champion Zhai Wei, leading twenty thousand horsemen, to campaign against the Tuyuhun chief Shipi; they reached Duzhou River and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou, Murong Yun, and Zhai Wei led twenty thousand horse against Tuyuhun chief Shipi, crushing him at Duzhou River.

sentences.zh: 視羆遁保白蘭山，遣使謝罪，貢其方物，以子宕豈為質。

translations.literal: Shipi fled to hold Baolan Mountain, sent envoys to apologize, presented tribute goods, and offered his son Dangqi as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Shipi fled to Baolan Mountain, sued for peace with tribute, and sent his son Dangqi as hostage.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑疊掘河內率屍五千，自魏降乾歸。

translations.literal: The Xianbei chief Dieju Henai led five thousand households from Wei to surrender to Gangui.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei chief Dieju Henai defected from Wei with five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 乾歸所居南景門崩，惡之，遂遷于苑川。

translations.literal: The Nanjing Gate where Gangui dwelt collapsed; he took it as ill omen and moved to Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing Gate of his residence collapsed; deeming it ill-omened, he moved to Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 姚興將姚碩德率眾五萬伐之，入自南安峽。

translations.literal: Yao Xing's general Yao Shuode led a host of fifty thousand to attack him, entering by Nan'an Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode of Later Qin invaded with fifty thousand men through Nan'an Gorge.

sentences.zh: 乾歸次於隴西以距碩德。

translations.literal: Gangui encamped at Longxi to oppose Shuode.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui took position in Longxi to block him.

sentences.zh: 興潛師繼發。

translations.literal: Xing secretly sent another army in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing followed with a second army in secret.

sentences.zh: 乾歸聞興將到，謂諸將曰：「吾自開建以來，屢摧勍敵，乘機籍算，舉無遺策。

translations.literal: Gangui heard that Xing was about to arrive and said to his generals: "Since I began building the state I have repeatedly crushed fierce enemies, seized opportunities by calculation, and undertaken nothing without a plan left over.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui told his captains: "Since I rose I have beaten every foe by timing and calculation.

sentences.zh: 今姚興盡中國之師，軍勢甚盛。

translations.literal: Now Yao Xing has brought the armies of the Middle Kingdom; his military momentum is very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yao Xing brings the full strength of the north—his host is immense.

sentences.zh: 山川阻狹，無從騎之地，宜引師平川，伺其怠而擊之。

translations.literal: Mountains and rivers are narrow and cramped; there is no ground for horse—we ought to lead the army onto level ground and strike when they grow slack."
translations.idiomatic: These narrows forbid cavalry—draw him to open ground and strike when he tires."

sentences.zh: 存亡之機，在斯一舉，卿等戮力勉之。

translations.literal: "The moment of survival or ruin lies in this one stroke; you must all exert your strength and strive."
translations.idiomatic: Our fate hangs on this battle—give me everything you have."

sentences.zh: 若梟翦姚興，關中之地盡吾有也。

translations.literal: "If we capture and cut down Yao Xing, the lands within the Pass will all be ours."
translations.idiomatic: Slay Yao Xing and the Pass country is ours."

sentences.zh: 」於是遣其衛軍慕容允率中軍二萬遷于柏陽，鎮軍羅敦將外軍四萬遷于侯辰穀，乾歸自率輕騎數千候興軍勢。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent Guard of the Host Murong Yun with the central army of twenty thousand to move to Baiyang, General Who Pacifies the Army Luo Dun with the outer army of forty thousand to move to Houchen Valley, and Gangui himself led several thousand light horse to watch Xing's military momentum.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Murong Yun with twenty thousand center troops at Baiyang, Luo Dun with forty thousand on the flank at Houchen Valley, and himself scouted with light horse.

sentences.zh: 俄而大風昏霧，遂與中軍相失，為興追騎所逼，入於外軍。

translations.literal: Before long a great wind brought dark fog; he lost contact with the central army and was pressed by Xing's pursuing horse, entering into the outer army.
translations.idiomatic: A gale and fog cut him off from the center; Xing's pursuers drove him into the outer wing.

sentences.zh: 旦而交戰，為興所敗。

translations.literal: At dawn they joined battle and were defeated by Xing.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they fought and Xing broke them.

sentences.zh: 乾歸遁還苑川，遂走金城，謂諸豪帥曰：「吾才非命世，謬為諸君所推，心存撥亂，而德非時雄，叨竊名器，年逾一紀，負乘致寇，傾喪若斯！

translations.literal: Gangui fled back to Yuanchuan, then ran to Jincheng, and said to the tribal chiefs: "My talent is not that of one destined for the age; wrongly have you all pushed me. My heart wished to set the realm right, yet my virtue is not that of a hero of the time; I presumptuously stole name and office for more than a decade—bearing a burden I invited the bandit, and ruin came like this!
translations.idiomatic: Gangui fled to Jincheng and told his chiefs: "I am no heaven-sent king—years of stolen titles have brought us to ruin.

sentences.zh: 今人眾已散，勢不得安，吾欲西保允吾，以避其鋒。

translations.literal: Now the host is scattered and the situation cannot be secure; I wish to go west and hold Yunwu to avoid their edge."
translations.idiomatic: The army is shattered—I will shelter in Yunwu and avoid their edge."

sentences.zh: 若方軌西邁，理難俱濟，卿等宜安土降秦，保全妻子。

translations.literal: "If you march west on the same road it will be hard for all to survive together; you ought to settle on your lands and submit to Qin, preserving wives and children."
translations.idiomatic: March west with me and few will survive—stay, submit to Qin, and keep your families."

sentences.zh: 」群下咸曰：「昔古公杖策，豳人歸懷；

translations.literal: " The subordinates all said: "In old times Duke Gu of antiquity leaned on his staff and the people of Bin came to his heart;
translations.idiomatic: His men answered: "When the ancient duke went west the people followed;

sentences.zh: 玄德南奔，荊、楚繈負。

translations.literal: Xuande fled south and Jing and Chu carried their children on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: when Liu Bei fled south Jing and Chu bore children on their backs for him.

sentences.zh: 分岐之感，古人所悲，況臣等義深父子，而有心離背！

translations.literal: The pain of parting ways is what men of old mourned—how much more we, whose bond with you is deep as father and son, yet would turn our hearts to desertion!
translations.idiomatic: Parting grieved the ancients—how can we, bound to you as sons, abandon you now!

sentences.zh: 請死生與陛下俱。

translations.literal: We beg to live and die together with your majesty."
translations.idiomatic: We will live and die with you."

sentences.zh: 」乾歸曰：「自古無不亡之國，廢興命也。

translations.literal: " Gangui said: "From antiquity there has been no state that did not perish; rise and fall are fate.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui said: "No realm lasts forever—rise and fall are fate.

sentences.zh: 苟天未亡我，冀興復有期。

translations.literal: If Heaven has not yet destroyed me, I hope there is a term for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven still favors us, we may rise again.

sentences.zh: 德之不建，何為俱死！

translations.literal: Since virtue was not established, why die together!
translations.idiomatic: Without virtue to save us, why drag you to death?

sentences.zh: 公等自愛，吾將寄食以終餘年。

translations.literal: You should each love yourselves; I shall live out my years by depending on others for food."
translations.idiomatic: Save yourselves—I will live out my days as a guest."

sentences.zh: 」於是大哭而別，乃率騎數百馳至允吾，禿髮利鹿孤遣弟傉檀迎乾歸，處之于晉興。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he wept greatly and parted; then he led several hundred horsemen galloping to Yunwu, and Tufa Lilugu's younger brother Rutan welcomed Gangui and lodged him at Jinxing.
translations.idiomatic: He wept and rode off with a few hundred horse to Yunwu; Tufa Lilugu's brother Rutan received him at Jinxing.

sentences.zh: 南羌梁戈等遣使招之。

translations.literal: The Southern Qiang chief Liang Ge and others sent envoys to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Qiang chiefs including Liang Ge sent envoys inviting him.

sentences.zh: 乾歸將叛，謀泄，利鹿孤遣弟吐雷屯於捫天嶺。

translations.literal: Gangui was about to rebel; the plot leaked, and Lilugu sent his younger brother Tulei to encamp at Mentian Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: A plot to rebel leaked; Lilugu sent his brother Tulei to block Mentian Ridge.

sentences.zh: 乾歸懼為利鹿孤所害，謂其子熾磐曰：「吾不能負荷大業，致茲顛覆。

translations.literal: Gangui, fearing Lilugu would harm him, said to his son Chipan: "I could not bear the great enterprise and brought it to this collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Lilugu, Gangui told Chipan: "I failed the realm and brought us to ruin.

sentences.zh: 以利鹿孤義兼姻好，冀存脣齒之援，方乃忘義背親，謀人父子，忌吾威名，勢不全立。

translations.literal: I thought Lilugu, with righteousness joined to marriage kinship, would preserve lip-and-tooth aid, yet he forgot righteousness and betrayed kin, plotting against father and son; he envies my renown and I cannot long stand secure.
translations.idiomatic: I trusted Lilugu's kinship bond, yet he turned on us—he will not let me live.

sentences.zh: 姚興方盛，吾將歸之。

translations.literal: Yao Xing is now ascendant; I shall go over to him."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing is ascendant—I will submit to him."

sentences.zh: 若其俱去，必為追騎所及。

translations.literal: If we all leave together we are sure to be overtaken by pursuing horse.
translations.idiomatic: If we flee together pursuers will catch us.

sentences.zh: 今送汝兄弟及汝母為質，彼必不疑。

translations.literal: Now I send you brothers and your mother as hostages; they will surely not doubt me.
translations.idiomatic: Send you, your brothers, and your mother as hostages—they will trust that I stay.

sentences.zh: 吾既在秦，終不害汝。

translations.literal: Once I am in Qin they will never harm you in the end."
translations.idiomatic: In Qin they will not harm you."

sentences.zh: 」於是送熾磐兄弟于西平，乾歸遂奔長安。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent Chipan and his brothers to Xiping; Gangui then fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chipan and his brothers to Xiping and fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 姚興見而大悅，署乾歸持節、都督河南諸軍事、鎮遠將軍、河州刺史、歸義侯，遣乾歸還鎮苑川，盡以部眾配之。

translations.literal: Yao Xing saw him and was greatly pleased; he appointed Gangui Bearer of the Staff, Commander of the Henan Armies, General Who Pacifies the Distant, Governor of Hezhou, and Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness, and sent Gangui back to garrison Yuanchuan, assigning him all his tribal following.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing received him gladly, named him Commander of Henan armies and Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness, and sent him back to Yuanchuan with his whole following.

sentences.zh: 乾歸既至苑川，以邊芮為長史，王松壽為司馬，公卿大將已下悉降號為偏裨。

translations.literal: When Gangui reached Yuanchuan he made Bian Rui chief clerk and Wang Songshou marshal; dukes, ministers, and great generals downward all had their titles reduced to subordinate ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanchuan he kept Bian Rui and Wang Songshou as staff and demoted his former court to subordinate ranks.

sentences.zh: ，熾磐自西平奔長安，姚興以為振忠將軍、興晉太守。

translations.literal: , Chipan fled from Xiping to Chang'an; Yao Xing made him General Who Quells Loyalty and Governor of Xingjin.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan fled Xiping to Chang'an; Yao Xing made him General Who Quells Loyalty and Governor of Xingjin.

sentences.zh: 尋遣使者加乾歸散騎常侍、左賢王。

translations.literal: Before long he sent envoys to add Gangui as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: Soon envoys advanced Gangui to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Worthy King.

sentences.zh: 遣隨興將齊難迎呂隆於河西，討叛羌党龍頭於滋川，攻楊盛將苻帛于皮氏堡，並克之。

translations.literal: He sent the general who followed Xing, Qi Nan, to welcome Lü Long in Hexi, campaigned against the rebel Qiang chief Longtou at Zichuan, and attacked Yang Sheng's general Fu Bo at Pishi Fort—all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Nan welcomed Lü Long in Hexi, crushed the Qiang rebel Longtou at Zichuan, and took Yang Sheng's Fu Bo at Pishi Fort.

sentences.zh: 又破吐谷渾將大孩，俘獲萬餘人而還。

translations.literal: He again defeated the Tuyuhun general Dahai and captured more than ten thousand in returning.
translations.idiomatic: He beat Tuyuhun general Dahai and returned with more than ten thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 尋復率眾攻楊盛將楊玉于西陽堡，克之。

translations.literal: Before long he again led his masses to attack Yang Sheng's general Yang Yu at Xiyang Fort and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took Yang Sheng's Yang Yu at Xiyang Fort.

sentences.zh: 既而苑川地震裂生毛，狐雉入於寢內，乾歸甚惡之。

translations.literal: Before long Yuanchuan was riven by earthquake and grew hair; foxes and pheasants entered the sleeping quarters—Gangui was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Earthquake split Yuanchuan and strange hair sprouted; foxes and pheasants entered his chamber—Gangui was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 姚興慮乾歸終為西州之患，因其朝也，興留為主客尚書，以熾磐為建武將軍、行西夷校尉，監撫其眾。

translations.literal: Yao Xing feared Gangui would in the end become a scourge of the western provinces; when Gangui came to court Xing detained him as Director of the Ministry of Guests, making Chipan General Who Establishes Martial Power and Acting Commandant of the Western Yi to oversee and pacify the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing detained Gangui at court as Director of the Ministry of Guests and left Chipan as Acting Commandant of the Western Yi to rule the tribes.

sentences.zh: 熾磐以長安兵亂將始，乃招結諸部二萬七千，築城-{于}-嵻㟍山以據之。

translations.literal: Chipan, because turmoil was beginning among the Chang'an troops, then summoned and gathered the various divisions—twenty-seven thousand—and built a city at Langlang Mountain to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: As Chang'an slid into chaos Chipan rallied twenty-seven thousand clansmen and fortified Langlang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 熾磐攻克枹罕，遣使告之，乾歸奔還苑川。

translations.literal: Chipan captured Fuhan and sent envoys to report it; Gangui ran back to Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan took Fuhan and summoned Gangui home to Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑悅大堅有眾五千，自龍馬苑降乾歸。

translations.literal: The Xianbei chief Yuedajian had a following of five thousand and surrendered to Gangui from Longma Park.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei chief Yuedajian defected from Longma Park with five thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 乾歸遂如枹罕，留熾磐鎮之。

translations.literal: Gangui then went to Fuhan and left Chipan to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui moved to Fuhan and left Chipan to hold it.

sentences.zh: 乾歸收眾三萬，遷於度堅山。

translations.literal: Gangui gathered a host of thirty thousand and moved to Dujian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered thirty thousand and relocated to Dujian Mountain.

sentences.zh: 群下勸乾歸稱王，乾歸以寡弱弗許。

translations.literal: The subordinates urged Gangui to style himself king; Gangui, because he was few and weak, would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged kingship; Gangui, deeming himself too weak, refused.

sentences.zh: 固請曰：「夫道應符曆，雖廢必興；

translations.literal: They pressed him firmly: "The Way responds to the calendar—though abolished it must rise again;
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him: "When the mandate shifts, fallen houses rise again;

sentences.zh: 圖籙所棄，雖成必敗。

translations.literal: what the charts and registers abandon, though established must perish."
translations.idiomatic: what heaven abandons, though strong must fall."

sentences.zh: 本初之眾，非不多也，魏武運籌，四州瓦解。

translations.literal: The host of Benchu was not few, yet Cao Wu by stratagem made the four provinces collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's host was vast, yet Cao Cao shattered four provinces by wit.

sentences.zh: 尋、邑之兵，非不盛也，世祖龍申，亡新鳥散。

translations.literal: The armies of Xun and Yi were not unstrengthened, yet Emperor Guangwu rose like a dragon and Xin-Mang scattered like birds.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang's armies were huge, yet Guangwu scattered them like birds.

sentences.zh: 固天命不可虛邀，符籙不可妄冀。

translations.literal: Truly Heaven's mandate cannot be sought in vain, nor can talismans and registers be hoped for rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate is not won by wish alone.

sentences.zh: 姚數將終，否極斯泰，乘機撫運，實系聖人。

translations.literal: Yao's number is about to end; denial reaches its peak and peace follows—seizing the moment to soothe fortune truly rests with a sage."
translations.idiomatic: Yao's house is spent—fortune turns to you; seize it, sage king."

sentences.zh: 今見眾三萬，足可以疆理秦、隴，清蕩洮河。

translations.literal: Now we see a host of thirty thousand, sufficient to order Qin and Long, and clear and pacify the Tao and He rivers.
translations.idiomatic: With thirty thousand men you can govern Qin and Long and sweep the Tao and He.

sentences.zh: 陛下應運再興，四海鵠望，豈宜固守謙沖，不以社稷為本！

translations.literal: Your majesty responds to the turning of fortune and rises anew; the four seas crane their necks in hope—how can you cling to modesty and not take the altars of state as your foundation!
translations.idiomatic: Fortune calls you back and the realm watches—do not cling to humility when the throne is at stake!

sentences.zh: 願時即大位，允副群心。

translations.literal: We beg that you take the great position at once, fulfilling the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Take the throne now and satisfy the people's hope.

sentences.zh: 」乾歸從之。

translations.literal: Gangui followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui agreed.

sentences.zh: 義熙三年，僭稱秦王，赦其境內，改元更始，置百官，公卿已下皆復本位。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yixi he presumptuously styled himself King of Qin, granted amnesty within his borders, changed the era name to Gengshi, established the hundred offices, and dukes and ministers downward all resumed their former ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi year 3 he proclaimed himself King of Qin, amnestied the realm, adopted the era Gengshi, restored his court, and returned officers to their former ranks.

sentences.zh: 遣熾磐討諭薄地延，師次煩於，地延率眾出降，署為尚書，徙其部落于苑川。

translations.literal: He sent Chipan to campaign against Yubodi Yan; the army halted at Fanyu; Diyan led his masses out to surrender and was appointed Director of the Secretariat, his tribe moved to Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan subdued Yubodi Yan at Fanyu; Diyan surrendered and was named Director of the Secretariat, his clan resettled at Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 又遣隴西羌昌何攻克姚興金城郡，以其驍騎乞伏務和為東金城太守。

translations.literal: He also sent the Longxi Qiang chief Chang He to capture Yao Xing's Jincheng commandery and made the fierce horseman Qifu Wuhe Eastern Jincheng Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Chang He took Yao Xing's Jincheng; Gangui made the Qiang horseman Qifu Wuhe its eastern administrator.

sentences.zh: 乾歸復都苑川，又攻克興略陽、南安、隴西諸郡，徙二萬五千戶于苑川、枹罕。

translations.literal: Gangui again made Yuanchuan his capital and also captured Xing's Lueyang, Nan'an, and Longxi commanderies, moving twenty-five thousand households to Yuanchuan and Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: He moved the capital back to Yuanchuan, seized Lueyang, Nan'an, and Longxi from Yao Xing, and resettled twenty-five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 姚興力未能西討，恐更為邊害，遣使署乾歸使持節、散騎常侍、都督隴西嶺北匈奴雜胡諸軍事、征西大將軍、河州牧、大單于、河南王。

translations.literal: Yao Xing lacked strength to campaign west and feared further border harm; he sent envoys to appoint Gangui Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander of the Longxi and Lingbei Xiongnu and Various Hu Armies, General Who Campaigns West, Governor of Hezhou, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to strike west, Yao Xing invested Gangui with grand titles including Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 乾歸方圖河右，權宜受之，遂稱籓於興。

translations.literal: Gangui was then plotting the right bank of the Yellow River and for the moment accepted, declaring himself a vassal of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Plotting the Hexi, Gangui accepted and feigned vassalage to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 遣熾磐與其次子中軍審虔率步騎一萬伐禿髮傉檀，師濟河，敗傉檀太子武台于嶺南，獲牛馬十餘萬而還。

translations.literal: He sent Chipan and his second son, Central Army Shenqian, with ten thousand foot and horse to campaign against Tufa Rutan; crossing the river they defeated Rutan's heir Wutai south of the ridge, capturing more than a hundred thousand cattle and horses on return.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan and Shenqian crossed the river, beat Tufa Rutan's son Wutai, and drove off vast herds.

sentences.zh: 又攻克興別將姚龍于伯陽堡，王憬於永洛城，徙四千餘戶于苑川，三千餘戶于譚郊。

translations.literal: He also captured Yao Xing's detached general Yao Long at Boyang Fort and Wang Jing at Yongluo City, moving more than four thousand households to Yuanchuan and more than three thousand to Tanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: He took Yao Long at Boyang and Wang Jing at Yongluo, resettling thousands to Yuanchuan and Tanjiao.

sentences.zh: 乾歸率步騎三萬征西羌彭利發於枹罕，師次於奴葵穀，利發棄其部眾南奔。

translations.literal: Gangui led thirty thousand foot and horse to campaign against the Western Qiang chief Peng Lifa at Fuhan; the army halted at Nukui Valley and Lifa abandoned his following and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui marched on Peng Lifa at Fuhan; Lifa fled south from Nukui Valley.

sentences.zh: 乾歸遣其將公府追及于清水，斬之。

translations.literal: Gangui sent his general Gongfu in pursuit to Qingshui and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu ran him down at Qingshui and took his head.

sentences.zh: 乾歸入枹罕，收羌戶一萬三千。

translations.literal: Gangui entered Fuhan and gathered twelve thousand Qiang households.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Fuhan he absorbed twelve thousand Qiang households.

sentences.zh: 因率騎二萬討吐谷渾支統阿若干於赤水，大破降之。

translations.literal: He then led twenty thousand horsemen to campaign against the Tuyuhun chief Zhitong Aqian at Chishui and routed and received his submission.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Tuyuhun Zhitong Aqian at Chishui and forced his surrender.

sentences.zh: 乾歸畋於五溪，有梟集於其手，甚惡之。

translations.literal: Gangui hunted at Wuxi; an owl perched on his hand—he took it as very ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting at Wuxi an owl settled on his hand—a dire omen.

sentences.zh: 六年，為兄子公府所弑，並其諸子十餘人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was assassinated by his nephew Gongfu, together with more than ten of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: In his sixth year his nephew Gongfu murdered him and more than ten of his sons.

sentences.zh: 公府奔固大夏，熾磐與乾歸弟廣武智達、揚武木奕於討之。

translations.literal: Gongfu fled to hold Gudu Daxia; Chipan with Gangui's younger brother Guangwu Zhida and Yangwu Muyiyu campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu fled to Daxia; Chipan, Zhida, and Muyiyu pursued him.

sentences.zh: 公府走，達等追擒於嵻㟍南山，並其四子，轘之于譚郊。

translations.literal: Gongfu fled; they pursued and seized him on Langlang South Mountain together with his four sons and executed them by cart-slicing at Tanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Gongfu on Langlang South Mountain with his four sons and executed the lot at Tanjiao.

sentences.zh: 葬乾歸於枹罕，偽諡武元王，在位二十四年。

translations.literal: Gangui was buried at Fuhan; his posthumous title was King Wuyuan; he had ruled twenty-four years.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Fuhan as King Wuyuan after twenty-four years on the throne.

sentences.zh: 乞伏熾磐

translations.literal: Qifu Chipan
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan (Western Qin)

sentences.zh: 熾磐，乾歸長子也。

translations.literal: Chipan was Gangui's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan, Gangui's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 性勇果英毅，臨機能斷，權略過人。

translations.literal: By nature he was brave, resolute, and heroic, decisive in the moment, with stratagems surpassing other men.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold, decisive, and strategically gifted beyond his peers.

sentences.zh: 初，乾歸為姚興所敗，熾磐質於禿髮利鹿孤。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gangui was defeated by Yao Xing, Chipan was a hostage with Tufa Lilugu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gangui fell to Yao Xing, Chipan was held hostage by Tufa Lilugu.

sentences.zh: 後自西平逃而降興，興以為振忠將軍、興晉太守，又拜建武將軍、行西夷校尉，留其眾鎮苑川。

translations.literal: Later he fled from Xiping and surrendered to Xing; Xing made him General Who Quells Loyalty and Governor of Xingjin, and also appointed him General Who Establishes Martial Power and Acting Commandant of the Western Yi, leaving his masses to garrison Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He escaped Xiping to Yao Xing, who gave him military command and left him at Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 及乾歸返政，復立熾磐為太子，領冠軍大將軍、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When Gangui returned to power he again made Chipan crown prince, Grand Champion General, Commander-in-Chief of Central and Outer Armies, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui restored him as crown prince and supreme commander with charge of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後乾歸稱籓于姚興，興遣使署熾磐假節、鎮西將軍、左賢王、平昌公，尋進號撫軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Later Gangui declared himself a vassal of Yao Xing; Xing sent envoys to appoint Chipan Acting Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, Left Worthy King, and Duke of Pingchang, and soon advanced him to General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yao Xing's suzerainty Chipan rose to General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 乾歸死，，熾磐襲偽位，大赦，改元曰永康。

translations.literal: When Gangui died, Chipan succeeded to the usurped throne, granted a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: On Gangui's death Chipan took the throne, proclaimed amnesty, and adopted the era Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 署翟勍為相國，麹景為御史大夫，段暉為中尉，弟延祚為禁中錄事，樊謙為司直。

translations.literal: He appointed Zhai Qing Chancellor, Qu Jing Censor-in-Chief, Duan Hui Commandant of the Center, his younger brother Yanzuo Recorder of Palace Affairs, and Fan Qian Director of Rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: He named Zhai Qing Chancellor, Qu Jing Censor-in-Chief, and filled the chief posts of state.

sentences.zh: 罷尚書令、僕射、尚書、六卿、侍中、散騎常侍、黃門郎官，置中左右常侍、侍郎各三人。

translations.literal: He abolished the offices of Director of the Secretariat, Vice Directors, Directors of the Six Ministries, Attendants-in-Ordinary, Regular Attendants, and Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate, and established Left and Right Regular Attendants and Gentlemen, three each.
translations.idiomatic: He simplified the secretariat and palace offices into paired attendants and gentlemen.

sentences.zh: ，遣其龍驤乞伏智達、平東王松壽討吐谷渾樹洛幹於澆河，大破之，獲其將呼那烏提，虜三千餘戶而還。

translations.literal: , He sent his Flying Dragon Qifu Zhida and Prince of Pingdong Wang Songshou to campaign against the Tuyuhun chief Shuluogan at Jiao River, routing him utterly, capturing his general Huna Wuti, and taking more than three thousand households on return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhida and Wang Songshou crushed Tuyuhun Shuluogan at Jiao River and brought back three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 又遣其鎮東曇達與松壽率騎一萬，東討破休官權小郎、呂破胡于白石川，虜其男女萬餘口，進據白石城，休官降者萬餘人。

translations.literal: , He also sent his General Who Pacifies the East Tanda with Wang Songshou leading ten thousand horsemen east to strike and defeat the Xiuguan chiefs Quan Xiaolang and Lü Pohu at Baishi River, capturing more than ten thousand men and women, advancing to hold Baishi City, and more than ten thousand Xiuguan submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tanda and Songshou beat Xiuguan chiefs at Baishi River, took ten thousand captives, and held the city.

sentences.zh: 後顯親休官權小成、呂奴迦等叛保白坑，曇達謂將士曰：「昔伯珪憑險，卒有滅宗之禍；

translations.literal: Later the Xiuguan chiefs of Xianqin, Quan Xiaocheng, and Lü Nujia, rebelled and held Bai Pit; Tanda said to officers and soldiers: "In old times Bo Gui relied on peril and in the end suffered the calamity of destroyed clan;
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuguan rebels held Bai Pit, Tanda warned: "Bo Gui trusted cliffs and lost his house—

sentences.zh: 韓約肆暴，終受覆族之誅。

translations.literal: Han Yue acted violently and in the end received the punishment of overturned clan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yue rampaged and his line was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 今小成等逆命白坑，宜在除滅。

translations.literal: Now Xiaocheng and the rest rebel at Bai Pit—they ought to be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: These men at Bai Pit must be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 王者之師，有征無戰，粵爾輿人，戮力勉之！

translations.literal: The king's army, when there is campaign, does not fight—strive, you men of the chariot, and exert yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: The king's host attacks without a fair fight—strike hard!"

sentences.zh: 」眾咸拔劍大呼，於是進攻白坑，斬小成、奴迦及首級四千七百，隴右休官悉降。

translations.literal: The multitude all drew swords and shouted; thereupon they advanced on Bai Pit, beheaded Xiaocheng, Nujia, and more than four thousand seven hundred heads, and all Xiuguan of Longyou submitted.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed Bai Pit, slew the chiefs and forty-seven hundred men, and Longyou Xiuguan submitted.

sentences.zh: 遣安北烏地延、冠軍翟紹討吐谷渾別統句旁於泣勤川，大破之，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: He sent Pacifier of the North Wudiyan and Champion Zhai Shao to campaign against the Tuyuhun detached chief Jubang at Qiqin River, routing him utterly and capturing a very great number.
translations.idiomatic: Wudiyan and Zhai Shao shattered Tuyuhun Jubang at Qiqin River with immense captures.

sentences.zh: 熾磐率諸將討吐谷渾別統支旁于長柳川，掘達於渴渾川，皆破之，前後俘獲男女二萬八千。

translations.literal: Chipan led his generals to campaign against the Tuyuhun detached chief Zhibang at Changliu River and Jueda at Kehun River, routing both, and before and after captured twenty-eight thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan himself broke Tuyuhun detachments at Changliu and Kehun Rivers, taking twenty-eight thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 僭立十年，有雲五色，起于南山，熾磐以為己瑞，大悅，謂群臣曰：「吾今年應有所定，王業成矣！

translations.literal: In the tenth year of his presumptuous reign, five-colored clouds arose from the southern mountain; Chipan took them as his own omen, was greatly pleased, and said to his ministers: "This year I ought to have something settled—the royal enterprise is accomplished!"
translations.idiomatic: In his tenth year five-colored clouds rose from the south; Chipan hailed them as his omen and told his court the kingship was secure.

sentences.zh: 」於是繕甲整兵，以待四方之隙。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired armor and marshaled troops, waiting for openings in the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: He armored his men and waited for chance in every quarter.

sentences.zh: 聞禿髮辱檀西征乙弗，投劍而起曰：「可以行矣！

translations.literal: Hearing that Tufa Rutan was campaigning west against the Yifu, he cast aside his sword and rose, saying: "We can march!"
translations.idiomatic: Learning Rutan had marched west against the Yifu, he sprang up: "Now we move!"

sentences.zh: 」率步騎二萬襲樂都。

translations.literal: He led twenty thousand foot and horse in a surprise strike on Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Ledu with twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 禿髮武台憑城距守，熾磐攻之，一旬而克。

translations.literal: Tufa Wutai relied on the city to resist; Chipan attacked and took it in ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Wutai held the walls; Chipan stormed Ledu in ten days.

sentences.zh: 遂入樂都，論功行賞各有差。

translations.literal: He then entered Ledu and distributed rewards for merit in varying grades.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Ledu and rewarded merit by rank.

sentences.zh: 遣平遠犍虔率騎五千追傉檀，徙武台與其文武及百姓萬餘戶於枹罕。

translations.literal: He sent Pacifier of the Distance Jian Qian with five thousand horsemen to pursue Rutan, moved Wutai with his civil and military officials and more than ten thousand households of the people to Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Qian pursued Rutan while Chipan deported Wutai and ten thousand households to Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 傉檀遂降，署為驃騎大將軍、左南公。

translations.literal: Rutan then surrendered; Chipan appointed him Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Zuonan.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan submitted and was named Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Zuonan.

sentences.zh: 隨傉檀文武，依才銓擢之。

translations.literal: For Rutan's civil and military officials he selected and promoted according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan's officials were placed by merit.

sentences.zh: 熾磐既兼傉檀，兵強地廣，置百官，立其妻禿髮氏為王后。

translations.literal: Chipan, having absorbed Rutan, was strong in soldiers and broad in territory; he established the hundred offices and made his wife of the Tufa clan queen.
translations.idiomatic: With Rutan absorbed Chipan was mighty; he crowned his Tufa wife and filled the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 十一年，熾磐攻克沮渠蒙遜河湟太守沮渠漢平，以其左衛匹逵為河湟太守，因討降乙弗窟乾而還。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Chipan captured Juqu Menxun's Hexi Administrator Juqu Hanping, made his Left Guard Pidi Hexi Administrator, and campaigned to receive the submission of the Yifu Kulian on return.
translations.idiomatic: He took Juqu Hanping, garrisoned Hexi, and reduced the Yifu Kulian.

sentences.zh: 遣其將曇達、王松壽等討南羌彌姐康薄于赤水，降之。

translations.literal: He sent his generals Tanda and Wang Songshou to campaign against the Southern Qiang chief Mijie Kangbo at Chishui and received his submission.
translations.idiomatic: Tanda and Songshou subdued Southern Qiang Mijie Kangbo at Chishui.

sentences.zh: 熾磐攻漒川，師次遝中，沮渠蒙遜率眾攻石泉以救之。

translations.literal: Chipan attacked Qiangchuan; the army halted at Diezhong; Juqu Menxun led his masses to attack Shiquan to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Menxun struck Shiquan to relieve Chipan's siege of Qiangchuan.

sentences.zh: 熾磐聞而引還，遣曇達與其將出連虔率騎五千赴之。

translations.literal: Chipan heard and withdrew, sending Tanda and his general Chulian Qian with five thousand horsemen to go to its aid.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan pulled back but sent five thousand horse under Tanda and Chulian Qian.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜聞曇達至，引歸，遣使聘於熾磐，遂結和親。

translations.literal: Menxun heard Tanda had arrived and withdrew, sending envoys to court Chipan; they then concluded a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Menxun retreated, sued for peace, and sealed a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 又遣曇達、王松壽等率騎一萬伐姚艾於上邽。

translations.literal: He also sent Tanda, Wang Songshou, and others with ten thousand horsemen to campaign against Yao Ai at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Tanda and Songshou marched ten thousand horse against Yao Ai at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 曇達進據蒲水，艾距戰，大敗之，艾奔上邽。

translations.literal: Tanda advanced and held Pu River; Ai resisted in battle and was routed utterly; Ai fled to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Tanda held Pu River, shattered Yao Ai, and drove him to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 曇達進屯大利，破黃石、大羌二戍，徙五千餘戶於枹罕。

translations.literal: Tanda advanced to encamp at Dali, broke Huangshi and Daxi forts, and moved more than five thousand households to Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Tanda took Dali, seized two forts, and resettled five thousand households at Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 令其安東木奕於率騎七千討吐谷渾樹洛幹於塞上，破其弟阿柴于堯扞川，俘獲五千餘口而還，洛幹奔保白蘭山而死。

translations.literal: He ordered his Pacifier of the East Muyiyu to lead seven thousand horsemen to campaign against the Tuyuhun chief Shuluogan on the frontier, defeated his younger brother Achai at Yaohan River, captured more than five thousand and returned, and Shuluogan fled to hold Baolan Mountain and died.
