translations.idiomatic: Muyiyu broke Shuluogan's brother at Yaohan; Shuluogan died on Baolan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 熾磐聞而喜曰：「此虜矯矯，所謂有豕白蹢。

translations.literal: Chipan heard and rejoiced: "This barbarian was fierce—the so-called boar with white hooves.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan rejoiced: "That fierce barbarian—the boar with white hooves—is gone."

sentences.zh: 往歲曇達東征，姚艾敗走；

translations.literal: In past years Tanda campaigned east and Yao Ai was defeated and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Tanda had already broken Yao Ai in the east;

sentences.zh: 今木奕於西討，黠虜遠逃。

translations.literal: now Muyiyu campaigned west and the cunning barbarian fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: Muyiyu has cleared the west.

sentences.zh: 境宇稍清，奸凶方殄，股肱惟良，吾無患矣。

translations.literal: The borders grow somewhat quiet, traitors and villains are being destroyed, and the limbs are all good—I have no worry."
translations.idiomatic: The realm quiets and my officers are true—I am at ease."

sentences.zh: 」於是以曇達為左丞相，其子元基為右丞相，麹景為尚書令，翟紹為左僕射。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made Tanda Left Chancellor, his son Yuanji Right Chancellor, Qu Jing Director of the Secretariat, and Zhai Shao Vice Director of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He named Tanda Left Chancellor, Yuanji Right Chancellor, Qu Jing Director of the Secretariat, and Zhai Shao Vice Director of the Left.

sentences.zh: 遣曇達、元基東討姚艾，降之。

translations.literal: He sent Tanda and Yuanji east to campaign against Yao Ai and received his submission.
translations.idiomatic: Tanda and Yuanji east subdued Yao Ai.

sentences.zh: 至是，乙弗鮮卑烏地延率戶二萬降於熾磐，署為建義將軍。

translations.literal: By this time the Yifu Xianbei Wudiyan led twenty thousand households to surrender to Chipan; Chipan appointed him General Who Establishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The Yifu chief Wudiyan surrendered with twenty thousand households and was named General Who Establishes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 地延尋死，弟他子立，以子軻蘭質于西平。

translations.literal: Wudiyan soon died; his younger brother Tazi succeeded and sent his son Kelan as hostage to Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudiyan died his brother Tazi sent his son Kelan as hostage to Xiping.

sentences.zh: 他子從弟提孤等率戶五千以西遷，叛於熾磐。

translations.literal: Tazi's younger cousin Tigui and others led five thousand households to migrate west, rebelling against Chipan.
translations.idiomatic: Cousins of Tazi led five thousand households west in revolt.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史出連虔遣使喻之，提孤等歸降。

translations.literal: The Liangzhou Inspector Chulian Qian sent envoys to instruct them; Tigui and the others returned and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chulian Qian's envoys brought Tigui back to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 熾磐以提孤奸猾，終為邊患，稅其部中戎馬六萬匹。

translations.literal: Chipan, because Tigui was treacherous and crafty and would in the end be a border scourge, levied sixty thousand war-horses from his division.
translations.idiomatic: Deeming Tigui treacherous, Chipan taxed his clan sixty thousand war-horses.

sentences.zh: 後二歲而提孤等扇動部落，西奔出塞。

translations.literal: Two years later Tigui and the others incited the tribes and fled west beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on Tigui stirred the tribes and fled beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 他子率戶五千入居西平。

translations.literal: Tazi led five thousand households to enter and dwell at Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Tazi entered Xiping with five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 先是，姚艾叛降蒙遜，蒙遜率眾迎之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yao Ai had rebelled and surrendered to Menxun; Menxun led his masses to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ai had defected to Juqu Menxun, who marched to receive him.

sentences.zh: 艾叔父俊言于眾曰：「秦王寬仁有雅度，自可安土事之，何為從涼主西遷？

translations.literal: Ai's uncle Jun spoke to the masses: "King Qin is broad and humane with elegant measure; one can settle on the land and serve him—why follow the Lord of Liang west in migration?"
translations.idiomatic: Ai's uncle Jun told the troops: "Chipan is merciful—why follow Menxun west?"

sentences.zh: 」眾咸以為然，相率逐艾，推俊為主，遣使請降。

translations.literal: The multitude all thought it right and in succession drove out Ai, pushing Jun as leader and sending envoys to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They expelled Ai, made Jun leader, and sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 熾磐大悅，征俊為侍中、中書監、征南將軍，封隴西公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Chipan was greatly pleased, summoned Jun as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Supervisor of the Secretariat, General Who Campaigns South, and Duke of Longxi with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan welcomed Jun as Duke of Longxi with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 使征西孔子討吐谷渾覓地于弱水南，大破之。

translations.literal: He sent his Campaigning West Confucius Zi to campaign against the Tuyuhun general Midi south of Ruoshui and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius Zi crushed Tuyuhun Midi south of the Weak River.

sentences.zh: 覓地率眾六千降於熾磐，署為弱水護軍。

translations.literal: Midi led six thousand of his masses to surrender to Chipan; Chipan appointed him Protector General of Ruoshui.
translations.idiomatic: Midi surrendered with six thousand men and was named Protector General of Ruoshui.

sentences.zh: 遣其左衛匹逵，建威梯君等討彭利和於漒川，大破之，利和單騎奔仇池，獲其妻子。

translations.literal: He sent his Left Guard Pidi, General Who Establishes Prestige Tijun, and others to campaign against Peng Lihe at Qiangchuan, routing him utterly; Lihe fled alone to Chouchi; they captured his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi and Tijun broke Peng Lihe at Qiangchuan; Lihe fled to Chouchi alone, his family taken.

sentences.zh: 徙羌豪三千戶於枹罕，漒川羌三萬餘戶皆安堵如故。

translations.literal: He moved three thousand Qiang chiefs to Fuhan; the more than thirty thousand households of Qiangchuan Qiang all dwelt in peace as before.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand Qiang elites went to Fuhan; thirty thousand Qiangchuan households were left unmolested.

sentences.zh: ，立其第二子慕末為太子，領撫軍大將軍、都督中外諸軍事，大赦境內，改元曰建弘，其臣佐等多所封授。

translations.literal: , He established his second son Moend as crown prince, General Who Pacifies the Army and Commander-in-Chief of Central and Outer Armies, granted amnesty within the borders, changed the era name to Jianhong, and his ministers and assistants received many enfeoffments and appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He named his second son Moend crown prince and supreme commander, amnestied the realm, adopted the era Jianhong, and enfeoffed his court.

sentences.zh: 熾磐在位七年而宋氏受禪，以宋元嘉四年死。

translations.literal: Chipan had ruled seven years when the Song house received the mandate; he died in the fourth year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years on the throne Chipan died in Yuanjia year 4 as the Song dynasty rose.

sentences.zh: 子慕末嗣偽位，在位四年，為赫連定所殺。

translations.literal: His son Moend succeeded to the usurped throne, ruled four years, and was killed by Helian Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Moend reigned four years before Helian Ding killed him.

sentences.zh: 始國仁以孝武僭位，至慕末四世，凡四十有六載而滅。

translations.literal: From the time Guoren presumptuously took the throne on Emperor Xiaowu to Moend, four generations in all, forty-six years in total, and then perished.
translations.idiomatic: From Guoren's first reign to Moend's death Western Qin lasted four generations and forty-six years.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫天地閉，大昆生；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When Heaven and Earth were closed, the great Kun were born;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When heaven and earth shut, the Kun arose;

sentences.zh: 雲雷屯，群凶作。

translations.literal: when cloud and thunder gathered, the many villains acted.
translations.idiomatic: when thunder rolled, villains multiplied.

sentences.zh: 自晉室遘孽，胡兵肆禍，封域無紀，干戈是務。

translations.literal: Since the Jin house met calamity, Hu armies wreaked disaster; within the realm there was no order and arms were the business.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court fell to barbarian armies and the realm knew only war.

sentences.zh: 國仁陰山遺噍，難以義服，伺我阽危，長其陵暴。

translations.literal: Guoren, a remnant morsel of the Yin Mountains, was hard to subdue by righteousness; watching our peril he grew in insolent violence.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren, a scrap of the northern wastes, preyed on Jin's weakness.

sentences.zh: 向使偶欽明之運，遭雄略之主，已當褫魂沙漠，請命槁街，豈暇竊據近郊，經綸王業者也。

translations.literal: Had he met the fortune of enlightened rule and a lord of heroic stratagem, he would already have lost his soul in the desert and begged life on the withered street—how could he have seized the near suburbs and woven kingly enterprise!
translations.idiomatic: Under a true emperor he would have died in the sands, not built a petty kingship.

sentences.zh: 乾歸智不及遠而以力詐自矜。

translations.literal: Gangui's wisdom did not reach far yet he prided himself on force and fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui lacked foresight yet trusted in force and deceit.

sentences.zh: 陷呂延之師，奸謀潛斷；

translations.literal: He trapped Lü Yan's army and secretly severed treacherous plans;
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed Lü Yan by ruse;

sentences.zh: 俘視羆之眾，威策遐舉。

translations.literal: he captured Shipi's masses and raised prestige by distant schemes.
translations.idiomatic: he humbled Tuyuhun by distant campaigns.

sentences.zh: 便欲誓湃、隴之餘卒，窺崤、函之奧區，秣疲馬而宵征，翦勍敵而朝食。

translations.literal: He then wished to swear the weary troops beyond the Tao and Long, spy on the hidden heartland of Xiao and Han, fodder tired horses for night marches, and cut fierce enemies for morning meals.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed of sweeping the Pass and striking the heartland on starving horses.

sentences.zh: 既而控弦嗚鏑，厥志未逞，沮岸崩山，其功已喪。

translations.literal: Soon he strung bows and whistling arrows yet his will was not fulfilled; riverbanks collapsed and mountains broke and his merit was already lost.
translations.idiomatic: His bows sang but his aim failed; omen and ruin followed.

sentences.zh: 履重氛於外難，幸以計全；

translations.literal: Treading heavy vapors in outer hardship, he luckily preserved himself by stratagem;
translations.idiomatic: He survived foreign wars by luck alone;

sentences.zh: 貽巨釁于蕭牆，終成凶禍，宜哉！

translations.literal: he left a great fault within the curtained hall and in the end met a violent end—fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: domestic treachery killed him—as he deserved.

sentences.zh: 熾磐叱吒風雲，見機而動，牢籠俊傑，決勝多奇，故能命將掩澆河之酋，臨戎襲樂都之地，不盈數載，遂隆偽業。

translations.literal: Chipan thundered in wind and cloud, saw the moment and moved, gathered heroes in his net, and won by many stratagems—thus he could order generals to cover the chiefs of Jiao River and himself take the field to strike the land of Ledu; in less than several years he swiftly raised a usurped enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan seized his moment, used daring captains, and in a few years built a great raid-kingdom.

sentences.zh: 覽其遺跡，盜亦有道乎！

translations.literal: Surveying his traces, even a robber had his Way!
translations.idiomatic: Even his conquests showed a robber's cunning discipline.

sentences.zh: 馮跋

translations.literal: Feng Ba
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba (Northern Yan)

sentences.zh: 馮跋，字文起，長樂信都人也，小字乞直伐，其先畢萬之後也。

translations.literal: Feng Ba, style Wengqi, was a man of Xindu in Changle; his childhood name was Qizhifa; his forebears were descendants of Bi Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba of Xindu in Changle, style Wengqi, childhood name Qizhifa, descended from Bi Wan.

sentences.zh: 萬之子孫有食采馮鄉者，因以氏焉。

translations.literal: Among Wan's descendants were those who received Feng Township as a fief and took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: A branch of Wan's line took Feng Township as fief and surname.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，跋祖父和避地上黨。

translations.literal: At the Yongjia turmoil Ba's grandfather He fled to settle in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongjia upheaval his grandfather He fled to Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 父安，雄武有器量，慕容永時為將軍。

translations.literal: His father An was martial and had capacity; under Murong Yong he served as a general.
translations.idiomatic: His father An was a warrior of parts and a general under Murong Yong.

sentences.zh: 永滅，跋東徙和龍，家于長穀。

translations.literal: When Yong perished, Ba moved east to Helong and made his home in Changgu.
translations.idiomatic: After Yong fell the family moved to Helong and settled at Changgu.

sentences.zh: 幼而懿重少言，寬仁有大度，飲酒一石不亂。

translations.literal: In youth he was grave and reserved, spoke little, was broad and humane with great magnanimity, and could drink a shi of wine without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was sober, sparing of speech, magnanimous, and could drink a shi without drunkenness.

sentences.zh: 三弟皆任俠，不修行業，惟跋恭慎，勤于家產，父母器之。

translations.literal: His three younger brothers were all knights-errant who did not cultivate proper conduct; only Ba was respectful and cautious, diligent in household production, and his parents prized him.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers were ruffians; only Ba was dutiful and diligent, and his parents favored him.

sentences.zh: 所居上每有雲氣若樓閣，時咸異之。

translations.literal: Where he dwelt, cloud-forms like towers and pavilions often appeared above the house, and at the time all thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Strange cloud-palaces often hung over his roof and neighbors marveled.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜見天門開，神光赫然燭於庭內。

translations.literal: Once at night he saw the Heavenly Gate open and divine light blaze brilliantly in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: One night he saw the Gate of Heaven open and divine light fill the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 及慕容寶僭號，署中衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao usurped the throne he appointed Ba Central Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao named him Central Guard General.

sentences.zh: 初，跋弟素弗與從兄萬泥及諸少年游于水濱，有一金龍浮水而下，素弗謂萬泥曰：「頗有見否？

translations.literal: Earlier, Ba's younger brother Sufu with his cousin Wanni and various youths played by the waterside; a golden dragon floated down on the water.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sufu and Wanni played by the river when a golden dragon floated past.

sentences.zh: 」萬泥等皆曰：「無所見也。

translations.literal: Sufu said to Wanni: "Did you see it?"
translations.idiomatic: Sufu asked Wanni: "Did you see it?"

sentences.zh: 」乃取龍而示之，咸以為非常之瑞。

translations.literal: Wanni and the others all said: "We saw nothing."
translations.idiomatic: They all said they had not.

sentences.zh: 慕容熙聞而求焉，素弗秘之，熙怒。

translations.literal: He then took the dragon and showed it to them; all considered it an extraordinary omen.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted the dragon for them—a marvel to all.

sentences.zh: 及即偽位，密欲誅跋兄弟。

translations.literal: Murong Xi heard and sought it; Sufu concealed it and Xi was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Xi demanded it; Sufu hid it and earned Xi's wrath.

sentences.zh: 其後跋又犯熙禁，懼禍，乃與其諸弟逃于山澤。

translations.literal: When Xi usurped the throne he secretly wished to execute the Ba brothers.
translations.idiomatic: On taking the throne Xi plotted to kill the Feng brothers.

sentences.zh: 每夜獨行，猛獸常為避路。

translations.literal: Later Ba again violated Xi's prohibition; in fear of disaster he fled with his brothers to mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Ba later broke Xi's law and fled to the hills with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 時賦役繁數，人不堪命，跋兄弟謀曰：「熙今昏虐，兼忌吾兄弟，既還首無路，不可坐受誅滅。

translations.literal: Each night he walked alone and fierce beasts always made way for him.
translations.idiomatic: He walked alone at night and beasts gave way.

sentences.zh: 當及時而起，立公侯之業。

translations.literal: At that time levies and corvée were numerous and people could not bear the command; the Ba brothers plotted: "Xi is now benighted and cruel and also envies our brothers—having returned there is no road for our heads; we cannot sit and receive execution.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes crushed the people; the brothers said: "Xi is mad and hates us—rise now or die later."

sentences.zh: 事若不成，死其晚乎！

translations.literal: We should seize the moment and rise, establishing the enterprise of duke and marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Let us seize the moment and build a princely house.

sentences.zh: 」遂與萬泥等二十二人結謀。

translations.literal: If the affair does not succeed, dying will only be late!"
translations.idiomatic: If we fail, we die anyway!"

sentences.zh: 跋與二弟乘車，使婦人禦，潛入龍城，匿于北部司馬孫護之室。

translations.literal: Thereupon they joined in conspiracy with Wanni and twenty-two others.
translations.idiomatic: They conspired with Wanni and twenty-two men.

sentences.zh: 遂殺熙，立高雲為主。

translations.literal: Ba and his two younger brothers rode in a carriage with women driving, secretly entered Longcheng, and hid in the house of the Northern Division Marshal Sun Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Ba entered Longcheng in a cart driven by women and hid with Sun Hu.

sentences.zh: 雲署跋為使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、征北大將軍、開府儀同三司、錄尚書事、武邑公。

translations.literal: They then killed Xi and established Gao Yun as lord.
translations.idiomatic: They slew Xi and raised Gao Yun.

sentences.zh: 跋宴群僚，忽有血流其左臂，跋惡之。

translations.literal: Yun appointed Ba Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief of Central and Outer Armies, General Who Campaigns North, Grand General with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Duke of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun invested Ba with the highest civil and military titles.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎王垂因說符命之應，跋戒其勿言。

translations.literal: Ba feasted the ministers; suddenly blood flowed on his left arm—Ba took it as ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: At a feast blood ran down his left arm—an ill sign.

sentences.zh: 雲為其幸臣離班、桃仁所殺，跋升洪光門以觀變。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Wang Chui thereupon spoke of the response of mandate; Ba warned him not to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chui spoke of destiny; Ba silenced him.

sentences.zh: 帳下督張泰、李桑謂跋曰：「此豎勢何所至！

translations.literal: Yun was killed by his favored ministers Liban and Taoren; Ba ascended Hongguang Gate to observe the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When favorites murdered Yun, Ba mounted Hongguang Gate to watch.

sentences.zh: 請為公斬之。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Tent Guard Zhang Tai and Li Sang said to Ba: "Where will this villain's momentum reach!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tai and Li Sang said: "We will cut them down for you."

sentences.zh: 」於是奮劍而下，桑斬班於西門，泰殺仁於庭中。

translations.literal: Please let us behead them for my lord."
translations.idiomatic: Grant us leave to strike."

sentences.zh: 眾推跋為主，跋曰：「范陽公素弗才略不恆，志於靖亂，掃清凶桀，皆公勳也。

translations.literal: Thereupon flourishing swords they descended; Sang beheaded Liban at the West Gate and Tai killed Taoren in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: They leapt down; Sang slew Liban, Tai killed Taoren.

sentences.zh: 」素弗辭曰：「臣聞父兄之有天下，傳之於子弟，未聞子弟籍父兄之業而先之。

translations.literal: The multitude pushed Ba as lord; Ba said: "Duke of Fanyang Sufu's talent and stratagem are not ordinary; his will is to quell turmoil and sweep away the vicious— all are your merits."
translations.idiomatic: The court urged Ba; he praised his brother Sufu's merit.

sentences.zh: 今鴻基未建，危甚綴旒，天工無曠，業系大兄。

translations.literal: Sufu declined: "I have heard that fathers and elder brothers who possess the realm pass it to sons and younger brothers; I have not heard of sons and younger brothers taking the enterprise of fathers and elder brothers first.
translations.idiomatic: Sufu refused: "The throne passes elder to younger—not the reverse."

sentences.zh: 願上順皇天之命，下副元元之心。

translations.literal: Now the great foundation is not yet established and peril hangs like a dangling tassel; Heaven's work admits no idleness and the enterprise rests on the eldest brother.
translations.idiomatic: The state is unsteady; Heaven favors my elder brother."

sentences.zh: 」群臣固請，乃許之，於是乙太元二十年乃僭稱天王于昌黎，而不徙舊號，即國曰燕，赦其境內，建元曰太平。

translations.literal: The ministers pressed firmly and he consented; in the twentieth year of the Taiping era he presumptuously styled himself Heavenly King at Changli without changing the old reign title; the state was called Yan, amnesty within the borders, era name Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by the court, in Taiping year 20 he proclaimed himself Heavenly King of Yan at Changli.

sentences.zh: 分遣使者巡行郡國，觀察風俗。

translations.literal: He separately sent envoys to tour the commanderies and states and observe customs.
translations.idiomatic: He sent inspectors to tour the realm and study local custom.

sentences.zh: 追尊祖和為元皇帝，父安為宣皇帝，尊母張氏為太后，立妻孫氏為王后，子永為太子。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his grandfather He as Emperor Yuan and his father An as Emperor Xuan, honored his mother Lady Zhang as Empress Dowager, made his wife Lady Sun empress, and his son Yong crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled his forebears, made Lady Sun empress, and Yong crown prince.

sentences.zh: 署弟素弗為侍中、車騎大將軍、錄尚書事，弘為侍中、征東大將軍、尚書右僕射、汲郡公，從兄萬泥為驃騎大將軍、幽平二州牧，務銀提為上大將軍、遼東太守，孫護為侍中、尚書令、陽平公，張興為衛將軍、尚書左僕射、永甯公，郭生為鎮東大將軍、領右衛將軍、陳留公，從兄子乳陳為征西大將軍、並青二州牧、上谷公，姚昭為鎮南大將軍、司隸校尉、上党公，馬弗勤為吏部尚書、廣宗公，王難為侍中、撫軍將軍、潁川公，自餘拜授，文武進位各有差。

translations.literal: He appointed his younger brother Sufu Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; Hong Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Campaigns East, Vice Director of the Right, and Duke of Ji; cousin Wanni Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of You and Ping; Wu Yinti Grand General and Liaodong Administrator; Sun Hu Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, and Duke of Yangping; Zhang Xing Guard General, Vice Director of the Left, and Duke of Yongning; Guo Sheng General Who Pacifies the East, Commander of the Right Guard, and Duke of Chenliu; cousin's son Ruchen General Who Campaigns West, Governor of Bing and Qing, and Duke of Shanggu; Yao Zhao General Who Pacifies the South, Colonel Director of the Masters of Writing, and Duke of Shangdang; Ma Fuqin Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Duke of Guangzong; Wang Nan Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Duke of Yingchuan; the rest received appointments and civil and military advancement in varying grades.
translations.idiomatic: He made Sufu Recorder of the Masters of Writing and General of Chariots and Cavalry, Hong Vice Director of the Right and Duke of Ji, Wanni Grand General of Agile Cavalry over You and Ping, and enfeoffed Sun Hu, Zhang Xing, Guo Sheng, Ruchen, Yao Zhao, Ma Fuqin, and Wang Nan—each to rank as merit allowed.

sentences.zh: 尋而萬泥抗表請代，跋曰：「猥以不德，謬為群賢所推，思與兄弟同茲休戚。

translations.literal: Before long Wanni submitted a memorial requesting replacement; Ba said: "I am unworthy and wrongly pushed by the worthies; I wish to share fortune and hardship with my brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Wanni asked to step down; Ba refused to divide the brothers' power.

sentences.zh: 今方難未寧，維城任重，非明德懿親，孰克居也！

translations.literal: Before long Wanni submitted a memorial requesting replacement; Ba said: "I am unworthy and wrongly pushed by the worthies; I wish to share fortune and hardship with my brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Wanni asked to step down; Ba refused to divide the brothers' power.

sentences.zh: 且折沖禦侮，為國籓屏，雖有他人，不如我弟兄，豈得如所陳也。

translations.literal: Now difficulty is not yet pacified and guarding the walls is a heavy charge—not bright virtue and kinship, who can occupy it!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still unsettled—only kin can hold the frontiers."

sentences.zh: 」於是加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Moreover repelling enemies and defending insult are the state's screen; though there were others, they were not like us brothers—how can it be as you stated."
translations.idiomatic: No stranger matches a brother on the border—your request cannot stand."

sentences.zh: ，跋下書曰：「昔高祖為義帝舉哀，天下歸其仁。

translations.literal: Thereupon he added Grand General with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced Wanni to Grand General with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 吾與高雲義則君臣，恩逾兄弟。

translations.literal: , Ba issued a writ: "In old times the High Ancestor mourned for Emperor Yi and the realm returned to his humanity.
translations.idiomatic: Ba decreed: "Gaozu mourned Emperor Yi and won the realm's heart."

sentences.zh: 其以禮葬雲及其妻子，立雲廟於韭町，置園邑二十家，四時供薦。」

translations.literal: I and Gao Yun were righteousness as ruler and minister, kindness surpassing brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun was my lord in name and my brother in kindness."

sentences.zh: 初，跋之立也，萬泥、乳陳自以親而有大功，謂當入為公輔，跋以二籓任重，因而弗征，並有憾焉。

translations.literal: Let Yun and his wife and children be buried with rites, establish Yun's temple at Jiuding, and set a park of twenty households with offerings in the four seasons."
translations.idiomatic: Bury Yun and his household with honor and maintain his temple at Jiuding."

sentences.zh: 乳陳性粗獷，勇氣過人，密遣告萬泥曰：「乳陳有至謀，顧與叔父圍之。

translations.literal: When Ba first rose, Wanni and Ruchen, because they were kin and had great merit, thought they should enter as chief ministers; Ba, because the two frontier posts were weighty, therefore did not summon them—and each harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Wanni and Ruchen expected the chief ministries; Ba left them on the frontier and bred resentment.

sentences.zh: 」萬泥遂奔白狼，阻兵以叛。

translations.literal: Ruchen was coarse and fierce, courage surpassing others; he secretly sent word to Wanni: "Ruchen has a supreme plan— I wish to plot with uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Ruchen secretly urged Wanni to rebel together.

sentences.zh: 跋遣馮弘與將軍張興將步騎二萬討之。

translations.literal: Wanni then fled to Bailang and blocked troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wanni fled to Bailang and rose in arms.

sentences.zh: 弘遣使喻之曰：「昔者兄弟乘風雲之運，撫翼而起。

translations.literal: Ba sent Feng Hong and General Zhang Xing with twenty thousand foot and horse to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Ba sent Hong and Zhang Xing with twenty thousand men against him.

sentences.zh: 群公以天命所鍾，人望攸系，推逼主上光踐寶位。

translations.literal: Hong sent envoys to instruct him: "Formerly we brothers rode the fortune of wind and cloud and spread wings to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Hong appealed to kinship: "We rose together by fortune."

sentences.zh: 裂土疏爵，當與兄弟共之，奈何欲尋干戈于蕭牆，棄友于而為閼伯！

translations.literal: The lords, because Heaven's mandate was concentrated and men's hopes attached, pushed the lord above to ascend the precious throne.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Ba king and split the realm among us."

sentences.zh: 過貴能改，善莫大焉。

translations.literal: Partitioning land and enfeoffing nobles ought to be shared with brothers—how seek dry blades within the curtained hall and abandon friendship to become Lord Yan!
translations.idiomatic: Why draw swords in the family and become enemies?"

sentences.zh: 宜舍茲嫌，同獎王室。

translations.literal: Passing faults can be corrected—nothing is greater than goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Repent and we stand together again."

sentences.zh: 」萬泥欲降，乳陳按劍怒曰：「大丈夫死生有命，決之於今，何謂降也。

translations.literal: You ought to set aside this suspicion and together aid the royal house."
translations.idiomatic: Cast off suspicion and serve the house together."

sentences.zh: 」遂克期出戰。

translations.literal: Wanni wished to surrender; Ruchen laid hand on sword in anger: "A great man's life and death have fate—let it be decided today; what is called surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: Wanni wavered; Ruchen drew his sword: "We fight, not kneel."

sentences.zh: 興謂弘曰：「賊明日出戰，今夜必來驚我營，宜命三軍以備不虞。

translations.literal: They then fixed the day to go out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: They marched to battle.

sentences.zh: 」弘乃密嚴人課草十束，畜火伏兵以待之。

translations.literal: Xing said to Hong: "The bandits will come out to battle tomorrow; tonight they are sure to come and alarm our camp—you ought to order the three armies to guard against the unexpected."
translations.idiomatic: Xing warned: "They will raid tonight—prepare."

sentences.zh: 是夜，乳陳果遣壯士千餘人來斫營。

translations.literal: Hong then secretly made men bind ten bundles of straw each and stored fire and ambush troops to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Hong stacked straw bundles and hid troops with fire.

sentences.zh: 眾火俱起，伏兵邀擊，俘斬無遺。

translations.literal: That night Ruchen indeed sent more than a thousand stalwarts to cut the camp.
translations.idiomatic: That night a thousand raiders struck the camp.

sentences.zh: 乳陳等懼而出降，弘皆斬之。

translations.literal: Fires rose together on all sides; ambush troops intercepted and attacked, capturing and beheading without remnant.
translations.idiomatic: Flames burst out; the ambush killed every raider.

sentences.zh: 署素弗為大司馬，改封遼西公，馮弘為驃騎大將軍，改封中山公。

translations.literal: Ruchen and the others, in fear, came out to surrender; Hong beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Terrorized, the rebels surrendered; Hong executed them.

sentences.zh: 跋下書曰：「自頃多故，事難相尋，賦役系苦，百姓困窮。

translations.literal: He appointed Sufu Grand Marshal and changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Liaoxi; Feng Hong Grand General of Agile Cavalry and changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Sufu became Grand Marshal of Liaoxi; Hong became Grand General of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 宜加寬宥，務從簡易，前朝苛政，皆悉除之。

translations.literal: Ba issued a writ: "Recently many troubles, affairs hard to follow in succession, levies and corvée tied in suffering, the hundred surnames impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: Ba proclaimed relief: "The people are exhausted—taxes must ease."

sentences.zh: 守宰當垂仁惠，無得侵害百姓，蘭台都官明加澄察。

translations.literal: There should be added broad pardon and effort from simplicity; harsh policies of the former court are all to be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Forgive debts and abolish Former Yan's harsh laws."

sentences.zh: 」初，慕容熙之敗也，工人李訓竊寶而逃，貲至巨萬，行貨于馬弗勤，弗勤以訓為方略令。

translations.literal: Guardians and magistrates should extend benevolence and favor and must not invade the hundred surnames; the Terrace and Ministry of Justice should clarify and inspect."
translations.idiomatic: Officials must rule justly; the censorate will watch."

sentences.zh: 既而失志之士書之于闕下碑，馮素弗言之於跋，請免弗勤官，仍推罪之。

translations.literal: When Murong Xi was defeated, the craftsman Li Xun stole treasure and fled, wealth reaching tens of millions, traveling goods to Ma Fuqin; Fuqin made Xun Strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun bribed Ma Fuqin and won office after Xi's fall.

sentences.zh: 跋曰：「大臣無忠清之節，貨財公行於朝，雖由吾不明所致，弗勤宜肆諸市朝，以正刑憲。

translations.literal: Before long disappointed men wrote on the stele below the gate; Feng Sufu spoke of it to Ba and requested Fuqin be removed from office and guilt pushed onto him.
translations.idiomatic: Slander appeared at the gate; Sufu demanded Fuqin's dismissal.

sentences.zh: 但大業草創，彝倫未敘，弗勤拔自寒微，未有君子之志，其特原之。

translations.literal: Ba said: "Ministers lack loyal and pure conduct and goods and wealth go publicly in court—though caused by my dimness, Fuqin ought to be displayed in the marketplace to correct penal law.
translations.idiomatic: Ba blamed court corruption yet spared Fuqin for the new state's sake.

sentences.zh: 李訓小人，污辱朝士，可東市考竟。

translations.literal: But the great enterprise is just begun and norms not yet ordered; Fuqin was raised from cold and humble station and had not the will of a gentleman—his person is especially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Fuqin was low-born and is forgiven.

sentences.zh: 」於是上下肅然，請賕路絕。

translations.literal: Li Xun is a petty man who defiled court gentlemen—he may be examined to the end at the eastern market."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun will die at the eastern market."

sentences.zh: 蝚蠕勇斛律遣使求跋女偽樂浪公主，獻馬三千匹，跋命其群下議之。

translations.literal: Thereupon above and below were stern; requests for bribes ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The court grew austere and bribery stopped.

sentences.zh: 素弗等議曰：「前代舊事，皆以宗女妻六夷，宜許以妃嬪之女，樂浪公主不宜下降非類。

translations.literal: The Rouran chief Hulu sent envoys requesting Ba's daughter as the false Princess of Lelang, presenting three thousand horses; Ba ordered his subordinates to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran chief sought Ba's daughter and offered three thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 」跋曰：「女生從夫，千里豈遠！

translations.literal: Sufu and the others deliberated: "Former dynasties' old affairs all took clan daughters to marry the six barbarians; it is fitting to promise a consort's daughter—the Princess of Lelang ought not descend to marry an alien kind."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers urged a lesser princess, not a royal daughter to barbarians."

sentences.zh: 朕方崇信殊俗，奈何欺之！

translations.literal: Ba said: "When a girl is born she follows her husband—a thousand li, how is it far!
translations.idiomatic: Ba said: "A daughter follows her husband—distance does not matter."

sentences.zh: 」乃許焉。

translations.literal: I am now exalting faith in alien customs—how can I deceive them!"
translations.idiomatic: I will not cheat our allies."

sentences.zh: 遣其遊擊秦都率騎二千，送其女婦於蝚蠕。

translations.literal: He then consented.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed.

sentences.zh: 庫莫奚虞出庫真率三千餘落請交市，獻馬千匹，許之，處之于營丘。

translations.literal: He sent his Raider Qin Du with two thousand horsemen to escort his daughter in marriage to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Du escorted the princess to the Rouran with two thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 分遣使者巡行郡國，孤老久疾不能自存者，振穀帛有差，孝悌力田閨門和順者，皆褒顯之。

translations.literal: Khitan and Kumo Xi of more than three thousand households requested market exchange, presenting a thousand horses; he consented and settled them at Yingqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan and Kumo Xi traded at Yingqiu with a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 昌黎郝越、營丘張買成、周刁、溫建德、何纂以賢良皆擢敘之。

translations.literal: He separately sent envoys to tour the commanderies and states; for the orphaned, aged, and long ill who could not support themselves he distributed grain and cloth in varying amounts; for filial piety, fraternal duty, diligent fields, and harmonious inner gates he all praised and displayed them.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors aided the needy and honored the virtuous.

sentences.zh: 遣其太常丞劉軒徙北部人五百戶于長谷，為祖父園邑。

translations.literal: Changli Hao Yue, Yingqiu Zhang Maicheng, Zhou Diao, Wen Jiande, and He Zuan, for worthiness, were all promoted and ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men of the realm received office.

sentences.zh: 以其太子永領大單于，置四輔。

translations.literal: He sent his Grand Steward Liu Xuan to move five hundred households of the northern people to Changgu as park-lands for his grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan resettled five hundred northern households as his grandfather's park.

sentences.zh: 跋勵意農桑，勤心政事，乃下書省徭薄賦，墮農者戮之，力田者褒賞，命尚書紀達為之條制。

translations.literal: He made his crown prince Yong hold the office of Grand Chanyu and established the Four Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Crown prince Yong became Grand Chanyu with Four Assistants.

sentences.zh: 每遣守宰，必親見東堂，問為政事之要，令極言無隱，以觀其志，於是朝野競勸焉。

translations.literal: Ba encouraged farming and sericulture and was diligent in government affairs; he then issued a writ reducing corvée and lightening levies, punishing those who neglected agriculture, rewarding those who worked fields, and ordered Director of the Secretariat Ji Da to make regulations for it.
translations.idiomatic: Ba promoted farming, cut taxes, and punished idlers.

sentences.zh: 先是，河間人褚匡言於跋曰：「陛下至德應期，龍飛東夏，舊邦宗族，傾首朝陽，以日為歲。

translations.literal: Whenever he sent out guardians and magistrates he always personally received them in the Eastern Hall, asked the essentials of governing affairs, ordered them to speak fully without concealment to observe their will—and thus court and countryside competed in encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: He interviewed every new magistrate in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 若聽臣往迎，致之不遠。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Hejian man Chu Kuang said to Ba: "Your majesty's supreme virtue responds to the season; the dragon flies in the eastern lands; the old homeland and clansmen all turn their heads to the morning sun, taking the day as a year.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Kuang offered to fetch kinsmen from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 」跋曰：「隔絕殊域，阻回數千，將何可致也？

translations.literal: If you hear me go to welcome them, bringing them is not far."
translations.idiomatic: Let me bring them—they are near by sea."

sentences.zh: 」匡曰：「章武郡臨海，船路甚通，出於遼西臨渝，不為難也。

translations.literal: Ba said: "Separated by a special region, blocked and turned back several thousand—how can they be brought?"
translations.idiomatic: Ba doubted the distance.

sentences.zh: 」跋許之，署匡遊擊將軍、中書侍郎，厚加資遣。

translations.literal: Kuang said: "Zhangwu commandery faces the sea; the ship route is very open, exiting from Liaoxi Linyu—not difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Kuang said ships from Zhangwu reach Linyu easily.

sentences.zh: 匡尋與跋從兄買、從弟睹自長樂率五千餘戶來奔，署買為衛尉，封城陽伯，睹為太常、高城伯。

translations.literal: Ba consented; he appointed Kuang Raider General and Attendant Secretariat Gentleman and richly sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Ba sent Kuang with rich support.

sentences.zh: 契丹庫莫奚降，署其大人為歸善王。

translations.literal: Before long Kuang with Ba's elder cousin Mai and younger cousin Du from Changle led more than five thousand households to flee and come; he appointed Mai Commandant of the Guard and Marquis of Chengyang, Du Grand Steward and Marquis of Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang returned with five thousand kinsmen; Mai and Du were ennobled.

sentences.zh: 跋又下書曰：「今疆宇無虞，百姓甯業，而田畝荒穢，有司不隨時督察，欲今家給人足，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Khitan and Kumo Xi submitted; he appointed their great chiefs as Kings Who Return to Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan and Kumo Xi chiefs became Kings Who Return to Goodness.

sentences.zh: 桑柘之益，有生之本。

translations.literal: Ba again issued a writ: "Now the borders are without worry and the hundred surnames are secure in their occupations, yet fields lie waste and the responsible offices do not inspect in season—wishing that every household be full and every man provided, is it not hard!
translations.idiomatic: Ba urged agriculture: "Fields lie fallow while people hunger."

sentences.zh: 此土少桑，人未見其利，可令百姓人殖桑一百根，柘二十根。

translations.literal: The benefit of mulberry and catalpa is the root of life.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberry and catalpa sustain life."

sentences.zh: 」又下書曰：「聖人制禮，送終有度。

translations.literal: This land has little mulberry; people have not seen its benefit—you may order the hundred surnames each to plant a hundred mulberry roots and twenty catalpa roots."
translations.idiomatic: Order every household to plant mulberry and catalpa."

sentences.zh: 重其衣衾，厚其棺槨，將何用乎？

translations.literal: He again issued a writ: "Sages institute rites and sending off the end has measure.
translations.idiomatic: Ba regulated funerals: "Sages set limits on mourning."

sentences.zh: 人之亡也，精魂上歸於天，骨肉下歸於地，朝終夕壞，無寒暖之期，衣以錦繡，服以羅紈，寧有知哉！

translations.literal: Heavy their clothes and quilts, thick their inner and outer coffins—what use is it?
translations.idiomatic: Why heap silks on the dead?"

sentences.zh: 厚於送終，貴而改葬，皆無益亡者，有損於生。

translations.literal: When men perish, the refined spirit returns above to Heaven and flesh and bone below to earth; by morning's end and evening's ruin there is no term of cold or warmth—clothing them in brocade and damask, serving them in gauze and silk, how can there be knowledge!
translations.idiomatic: The dead feel neither cold nor finery."

sentences.zh: 是以祖考因舊立廟，皆不改營陵寢。

translations.literal: Heavy in sending off the end, costly in changing burial—all without benefit to the dead and with harm to the living.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagant funerals harm the living."

sentences.zh: 申下境內，自今皆令奉之。」

translations.literal: Therefore ancestors followed the old in establishing temples, all without changing or rebuilding tomb palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Keep ancestral tombs as they were."

sentences.zh: 魏使耿貳至其國，跋遣其黃門郎常陋迎之於道。

translations.literal: He ordered throughout the borders that from now on all should follow this."
translations.idiomatic: The realm must obey these funeral rules."

sentences.zh: 跋為不稱臣，怒而不見。

translations.literal: Ba would not style himself a subject; Er was angry and would not receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Ba refused vassalage; Geng Er, enraged, refused audience.

sentences.zh: 及至，跋又遣陋勞之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Ba again sent Lou to comfort him with labor.
translations.idiomatic: When Er arrived Ba sent Chang Lou to greet him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 貳忿而不謝。

translations.literal: Er was resentful and did not thank him.
translations.idiomatic: Er fumed and gave no thanks.

sentences.zh: 跋散騎常侍申秀言於跋曰：「陛下接貳以禮，而敢驕蹇若斯，不可容也。

translations.literal: Ba's Attendant-in-Ordinary Shen Xiu said to Ba: "Your majesty received Er with rites, yet he dares be so arrogant and obstinate—he cannot be tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xiu urged: "You honored him, yet he insults you—he cannot stand."

sentences.zh: 」中給事馮懿以傾佞有幸，又盛稱貳之陵慠以激跋。

translations.literal: " Attendant of the Inner Palace Feng Yi, by fawning flattery enjoying favor, also greatly praised Er's insolence to provoke Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi flattered Er's arrogance to inflame Ba.

sentences.zh: 跋曰：「亦各其志也。

translations.literal: Ba said: "Each has his will.
translations.idiomatic: Ba said: "Each follows his own will."

sentences.zh: 匹夫尚不可屈，況一方之主乎！

translations.literal: Even a common man cannot be bent—how much more the lord of a region!"
translations.idiomatic: Even a commoner will not bow—how much more a regional lord!"

sentences.zh: 」請幽而降之，跋乃留貳不遣。

translations.literal: " They requested he be imprisoned and made to submit; Ba then detained Er and did not send him away.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to seize Er; Ba detained him.

sentences.zh: 是時井竭三日而復。

translations.literal: At that time the wells dried up for three days and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wells ran dry three days, then flowed again.

sentences.zh: 其尚書令孫護裏有犬與豕交，護見而惡之，召太史令閔尚筮之。

translations.literal: In his Director of the Secretariat Sun Hu's lane a dog mated with a pig; Hu saw it and took it as ill omen, summoning Grand Astrologer Min Shang to divine it.
translations.idiomatic: In Sun Hu's lane a dog coupled with a pig; Hu called Min Shang to divine the omen.

sentences.zh: 尚曰：「犬豕異類而交，違性失本，其于《洪範》為犬禍，將勃亂失眾，以至敗亡。

translations.literal: Shang said: "Dog and pig are different kinds yet mate—against nature and losing root; in the Hongfan it is the calamity of dogs; there will be sudden chaos, loss of the masses, and ruin unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Min Shang said: "This is the Dog Calamity of the Hongfan—rebellion and ruin follow."

sentences.zh: 明公位極塚宰，遐邇具瞻，諸弟並封列侯，貴傾王室，妖見裏庭，不為他也。

translations.literal: My lord's position reaches chief of the tombs; near and far all look up; your younger brothers are all enfeoffed as marquises, nobility overwhelming the royal house—the omen appears in the inner court and is not for others.
translations.idiomatic: The omen targets your house, my lord—not another."

sentences.zh: 願公戒滿盈之失，修尚恭儉，則妖怪可消，永享元吉。

translations.literal: I beg you guard against the fault of fullness, cultivate and esteem respectful thrift, and then the strange beings can be dispelled and you will forever enjoy supreme good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Guard against pride, practice thrift, and the omen will pass."

sentences.zh: 」護默然不悅。

translations.literal: Hu was silent and displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Hu listened in sullen silence.

sentences.zh: 昌黎尹孫伯仁、護弟叱支、叱支弟乙拔等俱有才力，以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: Changli Magistrate Sun Boren, Hu's younger brother Chizhi, and Chizhi's younger brother Yiba all had talent and strength and were known for fierce bravery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Boren, Chizhi, and Yiba of Sun Hu's clan were famed for valor.

sentences.zh: 跋之立也，並冀開府，而跋未之許，由是有怨言。

translations.literal: When Ba rose they all hoped for Grand General with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, but Ba did not grant it—hence they had complaints.
translations.idiomatic: They expected open Grand General appointments; Ba withheld them and bred resentment.

sentences.zh: 每于朝饗之際，常拔劍擊柱曰：「興建大業，有功力焉，而滯於散將，豈是漢祖河山之義乎！

translations.literal: At each court feast they would draw swords and strike pillars, saying: "In establishing the great enterprise we had merit, yet we stagnate as scattered generals—is this the righteousness of Han's ancestor sharing the rivers and mountains!"
translations.idiomatic: At court they struck pillars with swords: "We built this realm—where is our share of power?"

sentences.zh: 」跋怒，誅之。

translations.literal: " Ba was angry and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Ba had them executed.

sentences.zh: 進護左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司、錄尚書事以慰之。

translations.literal: He advanced Hu to Left Household Counsellor of the First Rank, Grand General with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Sun Hu to chief minister to appease him.

sentences.zh: 護自三弟誅後，常怏怏有不悅之色，跋怒，酖之。

translations.literal: After his three younger brothers were executed Hu was often displeased in expression; Ba was angry and poisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: After his brothers' deaths Hu glowered; Ba poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 尋而遼東太守務銀提自以功在孫護、張興之右，而出為邊郡，抗表有恨言，密謀外叛。

translations.literal: Before long Liaodong Administrator Wu Yinti, considering his merit above Sun Hu and Zhang Xing yet assigned to a frontier commandery, submitted a memorial with resentful words and secretly plotted external rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yinti, resenting a frontier post despite greater merit, plotted revolt.

sentences.zh: 跋怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Ba was angry and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ba executed him.

sentences.zh: 跋下書曰：「武以平亂，文以經務，甯國濟俗，實所憑焉。

translations.literal: Ba issued a writ: "Martial power pacifies chaos, civil culture orders affairs—truly what pacifies the state and aids custom relies upon these.
translations.idiomatic: Ba proclaimed: "By arms we pacify chaos; by culture we order the realm."

sentences.zh: 自頃喪難，禮崩樂壞，閭閻絕諷誦之音，後行無庠序之教，子衿之歎復興於今，豈所以穆章風化，崇闡斯文！

translations.literal: Recently in the calamity of loss, rites collapsed and music was ruined; lanes and wards lacked the sound of recitation and study, and the young had no school instruction—the sigh of the blue collar rises again today; how is this the way to harmonize standards and customs and exalt and spread this culture!
translations.idiomatic: Rites and schools lie in ruins—how can civilization endure?"

sentences.zh: 可營建太學，以長樂劉軒、營丘張熾、成周翟崇為博士郎中，簡二千石已下子弟年十五已上教之。」

translations.literal: You may establish the Imperial University, making Liu Xuan of Changle, Zhang Chi of Yingqiu, and Zhai Chong of Chengzhou Masters of the Doctorate, selecting sons of officials below two-thousand-shi rank aged fifteen and above to teach them."
translations.idiomatic: He founded a university under Liu Xuan, Zhang Chi, and Zhai Chong.

sentences.zh: 跋弟丕，先是因亂投於高句麗，跋迎致之，至龍城，以為左僕射、常山公。

translations.literal: Ba's younger brother Pi had earlier, because of turmoil, fled to Goguryeo; Ba welcomed and brought him, and when he reached Longcheng made him Vice Director of the Left and Duke of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Ba recalled his brother Pi from Goguryeo and made him Vice Director of the Left.

sentences.zh: 蝚蠕斛律為其弟大但所逐，盡室奔跋，乃館之於遼東郡，待之以客禮。

translations.literal: The Rouran Hulu was driven out by his younger brother Dandan and fled with his whole household to Ba; Ba then lodged them in Liaodong commandery and treated them with guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran Hulu, expelled by his brother, fled to Ba and was lodged as a guest in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 跋納其女為昭儀。

translations.literal: Ba took his daughter as Imperial Concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Ba took Hulu's daughter as consort.

sentences.zh: 時三月不雨，至於夏五月。

translations.literal: At that time for three months there was no rain, until the fifth month of summer.
translations.idiomatic: No rain fell for three months until summer's fifth month.

sentences.zh: 斛律上書請還塞北，跋曰：「棄國萬里，又無內應。

translations.literal: Hulu submitted a memorial requesting return north of the passes; Ba said: "Abandoning your state ten thousand li, moreover without inner support.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu begged to return north; Ba objected: "You are far from home without allies."

sentences.zh: 若以強兵相送，糧運難繼；

translations.literal: If strong troops escort you, grain transport is hard to continue;
translations.idiomatic: A large escort cannot be supplied;

sentences.zh: 少也，勢不能固。

translations.literal: if few, the momentum cannot hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: a small one cannot protect you."

sentences.zh: 且千里襲國，古人為難，況數千里乎！

translations.literal: Moreover to strike a state a thousand li away the ancients considered it hard—how much more several thousand li!"
translations.idiomatic: A thousand-li raid is perilous—how much more several thousand!"

sentences.zh: 」斛律固請曰：「不煩大眾，願給騎三百足矣。

translations.literal: " Hulu pressed firmly: "It will not trouble the great host; I wish only three hundred horsemen and that suffices.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu insisted: "Three hundred horse are enough."

sentences.zh: 得達敕勒國，人必欣而來迎。

translations.literal: Reaching the Tiele state, the people will surely rejoice and come to welcome.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele will welcome me home."

sentences.zh: 」乃許之，遣單于前輔萬陵率騎三百送之。

translations.literal: " He then consented and sent Former Chanyu Assistant Wanling with three hundred horsemen to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Ba sent Wanling with three hundred horse to escort him.

sentences.zh: 陵憚遠役，至黑山，殺斛律而還。

translations.literal: Ling feared the distant service; reaching Black Mountain he killed Hulu and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wanling feared the march, murdered Hulu at Black Mountain, and fled back.

sentences.zh: 晉青州刺史申永遣使浮海來聘，跋乃使其中書郎李扶報之。

translations.literal: Jin Governor of Qingzhou Shen Yong sent envoys by sea to court Ba; Ba then sent his Secretariat Gentleman Li Fu to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yong of Eastern Jin sent envoys by sea; Ba replied through Li Fu.

sentences.zh: 蝚蠕大但遣使獻馬三千匹，羊萬口。

translations.literal: The Rouran Dandan sent envoys presenting three thousand horses and ten thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran Dandan sent three thousand horses and ten thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 有赤氣四塞，太史令張穆言於跋曰：「兵氣也。

translations.literal: Crimson vapor filled the four quarters; Grand Astrologer Zhang Mu said to Ba: "It is the qi of soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Red mists filled the sky; Zhang Mu said: "This is martial qi."

sentences.zh: 今大魏威制六合，而聘使斷絕。

translations.literal: Now Great Wei's might controls the six directions, yet embassies are cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei rules all under heaven, yet we have cut off embassies."

sentences.zh: 自古未有鄰接境，不通和好。

translations.literal: From antiquity there has never been neighboring borders without communication and alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring states have always exchanged envoys."

sentences.zh: 違義怒鄰，取亡之道。

translations.literal: Violating righteousness and angering neighbors is the way to invite ruin.
translations.idiomatic: To defy a neighbor is to invite ruin."

sentences.zh: 宜還前使，修和結盟。

translations.literal: You ought to return the former envoy and repair harmony and alliance."
translations.idiomatic: Return their envoy and restore peace."

sentences.zh: 」跋曰：「吾當思之。

translations.literal: " Ba said: "I shall consider it."
translations.idiomatic: Ba said: "I will consider it."

sentences.zh: 」尋而魏軍大至，遣單于右輔古泥率騎候之。

translations.literal: " Before long Wei armies arrived in great force; he sent Right Assistant Chanyu Gunie with horsemen to reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: Wei armies came; Ba sent Gunie to scout.

sentences.zh: 去城十五里，遇軍奔還。

translations.literal: Fifteen li from the city they met the army and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen li from the city Gunie met Wei and fled.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將姚昭、皇甫軌等距戰，軌中流矢死。

translations.literal: He again sent his generals Yao Zhao, Huangfu Gui, and others to resist in battle; Gui was struck by a flying arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zhao and Huangfu Gui fought; Gui died of an arrow wound.

sentences.zh: 魏以有備，引還。

translations.literal: Wei, because there was preparation, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wei withdrew, finding Ba prepared.

sentences.zh: 跋境地震山崩，洪光門鸛雀折。

translations.literal: Within Ba's borders the earth quaked and mountains collapsed; the magpie-roost at Hongguang Gate broke.
translations.idiomatic: Earthquakes shook Ba's realm; the Hongguang Gate magpie perch snapped.

sentences.zh: 又地震，右寢壞。

translations.literal: Again the earth quaked and the right sleeping quarters were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Another quake destroyed the right palace quarters.

sentences.zh: 跋問閔尚曰：「比年屢有地動之變，卿可明言其故。

translations.literal: Ba asked Min Shang: "In recent years there have repeatedly been changes of earth movement—you can clearly state the reason."
translations.idiomatic: Ba asked Min Shang why the earth kept shaking.

sentences.zh: 」尚曰：「地，陰也，主百姓。

translations.literal: " Shang said: "Earth is yin and governs the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Min Shang said: "Earth is yin and rules the people."

sentences.zh: 震有左右，此震皆向右，臣懼百姓將西移。

translations.literal: Quakes have left and right; these quakes all move to the right—I fear the hundred surnames will shift west."
translations.idiomatic: These tremors lean west—I fear the people will migrate west."

sentences.zh: 」跋曰：「吾亦甚慮之。

translations.literal: " Ba said: "I too am greatly concerned."
translations.idiomatic: Ba said: "That worries me as well."

sentences.zh: 」分遣使者巡行郡國，問所疾苦，孤老不能自存者，賜以穀帛有差。

translations.literal: " He separately sent envoys to tour the commanderies and states, ask their afflictions, and for the orphaned and aged who could not support themselves distributed grain and cloth in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He sent inspectors to aid the needy with grain and cloth.

sentences.zh: 跋立十一年，至是，也，此後事入于宋。

translations.literal: Ba had ruled eleven years; at this time—also—after this affairs enter into Song.
translations.idiomatic: In his eleventh year—here the record passes to Song.

sentences.zh: 至死。

translations.literal: Until his death.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 弟弘殺跋子翼自立，後為魏所伐，東奔高句麗。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hong killed Ba's son Yi and usurped rule himself; later he was campaigned against by Wei and fled east to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Hong murdered Ba's son Yi and seized the throne; Wei drove him to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 居二年，高句麗殺之。

translations.literal: After two years Goguryeo killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo killed him two years later.

sentences.zh: 始，跋以孝武僭號，至弘二世，凡二十有八載。

translations.literal: From the time Ba presumptuously took the throne on Emperor Xiaowu to Hong, two generations in all, twenty-eight years in total.
translations.idiomatic: From Ba's first reign to Hong's fall Northern Yan lasted twenty-eight years.

translations.literal: Section divider in source text.

sentences.zh: 弟 素弗

translations.literal: Younger brother Sufu
translations.idiomatic: Sufu, younger brother

sentences.zh: =馮素弗，跋之長弟也。

translations.literal: Feng Sufu was Ba's eldest younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Sufu, Ba's eldest younger brother.

sentences.zh: 慷慨有大志，姿貌魁偉，雄傑不群，任俠放蕩，不修小節，故時人未之奇，惟王齊異焉，曰：「撥亂才也。

translations.literal: He was magnanimous with great resolve, imposing in appearance, heroic and not of the crowd, a knight-errant and unrestrained, not cultivating minor conduct—so men of the time did not think him extraordinary; only Wang Qi regarded him as different and said: "A talent for setting chaos aright.
translations.idiomatic: Sufu was bold and unruly; only Wang Qi called him a talent to quell chaos.

sentences.zh: 」惟交結時豪為務，不以產業經懷。

translations.literal: " He only made befriending the bold of the age his task and did not take household production to heart.
translations.idiomatic: He courted heroes and scorned property.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，自詣慕容熙尚書左丞韓業請婚，業怒而距之。

translations.literal: At weak cap he went on his own to Murong Xi's Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Han Ye to request marriage; Ye angrily refused him.
translations.idiomatic: He sought Han Ye's daughter; Ye refused in anger.

sentences.zh: 復求尚書郎高邵女，邵亦弗許。

translations.literal: He again sought the daughter of Secretariat Gentleman Gao Shao; Shao also would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shao likewise refused his suit.

sentences.zh: 南宮令成藻，豪俊有高名，素弗造焉，藻命門者勿納。

translations.literal: Nangong Magistrate Cheng Zao, a bold man of high renown—Sufu visited him; Zao ordered the gatekeeper not to admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zao, a famed hero, barred his gate.

sentences.zh: 素弗逕入，與藻對坐，旁若無人。

translations.literal: Sufu went straight in, sat opposite Zao, and was as if no one else were present.
translations.idiomatic: Sufu entered anyway and sat as an equal.

sentences.zh: 談飲連日。

translations.literal: They talked and drank for successive days.
translations.idiomatic: They talked and drank for days.

sentences.zh: 藻始奇之，曰：「吾遠求騏驥，不知近在東鄰，何識子之晚也！

translations.literal: Zao then marveled at him and said: "I sought a qi ji far away and did not know one was near in the eastern neighbor—how late I recognized you!
translations.idiomatic: Zao exclaimed: "I sought a steed afar while one stood next door!"

sentences.zh: 」當世俠士莫不歸之。

translations.literal: " Knights-errant of the age all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Every bold man of the age followed him.

sentences.zh: 及熙僭號，為侍御郎、小帳下督。

translations.literal: When Xi usurped the throne he served as Attendant Gentleman and minor Tent Guard Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Murong Xi he was an attendant and guard officer.

sentences.zh: 跋之偽業，素弗所建也。

translations.literal: Ba's usurped enterprise was what Sufu established.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Yan was Sufu's achievement.

sentences.zh: 及為宰輔，謙虛恭慎，非禮不動，雖廝養之賤，皆與之抗禮。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister he was humble, respectful, and cautious, not moving outside ritual; even menials of the lowest rank he faced with opposing rites.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he was humble even to servants.

sentences.zh: 車服屋宇，務於儉約，修己率下，百僚憚之。

translations.literal: Carriages, robes, houses, and halls he kept to thrift; cultivating himself he led those below and the hundred officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly and awed the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 初為京尹。

translations.literal: He first served as Capital Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He first governed the capital.

sentences.zh: 及鎮營丘，百姓歌之。

translations.literal: When he garrisoned Yingqiu the common people sang of him.
translations.idiomatic: At Yingqiu the people sang his praise.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂韓業曰：「君前既不顧，今將自取，何如？

translations.literal: Once he said to Han Ye: "Earlier you would not regard me; now I shall take for myself—what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: He told Han Ye: "You refused me once—now I take what I want."

sentences.zh: 」業拜而陳謝。

translations.literal: " Ye bowed and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Ye bowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 素弗曰：「既往之事，豈復與君計之！

translations.literal: Sufu said: "Past affairs—how can I reckon them with you again!
translations.idiomatic: Sufu said: "The past is past."

sentences.zh: 」然待業彌厚。

translations.literal: " Yet he treated Ye all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he treated Ye with greater kindness.

sentences.zh: 好存亡繼絕，申拔舊門，問侍中陽哲曰：「秦、趙勳臣子弟今何在乎？

translations.literal: He loved preserving what was dying and continuing what was cut off, promoting old houses; he asked Attendant-in-Ordinary Yang Zhe: "Where are the sons and younger brothers of Qin and Zhao merit families now?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Yang Zhe where the old Qin and Zhao noble lines had gone.

sentences.zh: 」哲曰：「皆在中州，惟桃豹孫鮮在焉。

translations.literal: " Zhe said: "All are in the central provinces; only Tao Bao's grandson Xian is here."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhe said only Tao Bao's grandson Xian remained in the east.

sentences.zh: 」素弗召為左常侍，論者歸其有宰衡之度。

translations.literal: " Sufu summoned him as Left Regular Attendant; discussants attributed to him the measure of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Sufu made Xian Left Regular Attendant; men said he had a chancellor's bearing.

sentences.zh: 跋之七年死，跋哭之哀慟。

translations.literal: In Ba's seventh year Sufu died; Ba wept for him in bitter grief.
translations.idiomatic: Sufu died in Ba's seventh year; Ba wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 比葬，七臨之。

translations.literal: Until the burial he visited the coffin seven times.
translations.idiomatic: Ba visited the coffin seven times before burial.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自五胡縱慝，九域淪胥，帝裏神州，遂混之於荒裔，鴻名寶位，咸假之於雜種。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Since the Five Hu ran riot, the nine domains were lost to ruin; the imperial capital and divine land were then mixed into the wild borderlands, and great name and precious throne were all lent to alien kinds.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The Five Hu ravaged the realm and barbarians seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂戎狄凶囂，未窺道德，欺天擅命，抑乃其常。

translations.literal: It was once said that Rong and Di were fierce and clamorous, not yet glimpsing the Way and virtue, deceiving Heaven and usurping mandate—indeed their constant.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians were said to know only force, not the Way.

sentences.zh: 而馮跋出自中州，有殊丑類，因鮮卑之昏虐，亦盜名於海隅。

translations.literal: Yet Feng Ba came forth from the central provinces, of a different ugly kind; riding on Xianbei benighted cruelty, he too stole a name on the sea corner.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Feng Ba was Chinese-born and stole a coastal throne amid Xianbei chaos.

sentences.zh: 然其遷徙之餘，少非雄傑，幸以寬厚為眾所推。

translations.literal: Yet among the remainder of his migration few were heroes; luckily he was pushed by the multitude through breadth and generosity.
translations.idiomatic: His clan were no heroes; the people raised him for his gentleness.

sentences.zh: 初雖砥礪，終罕成德，舊史稱其信惑妖祀，斥黜諫臣，無開馭之才，異經決之士，信矣。

translations.literal: At first he did hone himself, yet in the end he rarely achieved virtue; old histories say he believed perverse omens, expelled remonstrating ministers, had no talent for driving the chariot, and lacked men who decided by the classics—true indeed.
translations.idiomatic: He began well yet ended weak—credulous, hostile to counsel, no true king.

sentences.zh: 速禍致寇，良謂在茲。

translations.literal: Hastening calamity and inviting the bandit—truly it lay here.
translations.idiomatic: His faults brought swift disaster.

sentences.zh: 猶能撫育黎萌，保守疆宇，發號施令，二十餘年，豈天意乎，非人事也！

translations.literal: Yet he could nurture and rear the black-haired people, guard and preserve the borders, issue orders and decrees for more than twenty years—was it Heaven's intent? Not human affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he ruled gently twenty years—fate, not merit alone.

translations.literal: 【Praise】
translations.idiomatic: Praise.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：國仁驍武，乾歸勇悍。

translations.literal: The praise says: Guoren was martial; Gangui was brave and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Praise runs: Guoren was martial, Gangui fierce.

sentences.zh: 矯矯熾磐，臨機能斷。

translations.literal: Chipan towered in wind and cloud, saw the moment and acted.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan was bold and seized his hour.

sentences.zh: 孰謂獯虜，亦懷沈算。

translations.literal: Who says the Di barbarians do not also harbor deep designs.
translations.idiomatic: Even Di chieftains could scheme deeply.

sentences.zh: 文起常才，憑時叛換。

translations.literal: Wengqi was ordinary talent, relying on the season to rebel and change.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba was merely opportunistic talent.

sentences.zh: 咸竊大寶，為我多難。

translations.literal: All stole the great treasure, bringing many hardships upon us.
translations.idiomatic: They all usurped the throne and heaped calamity upon us.
